💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward have cast their net far and wide to find new players for Liverpool to target.
  • During the 2026-27 summer transfer window, over £150 million + was spent on upcoming players to try and bolster the Reds' ranks.
  • And, while some of them moves have worked out well, others haven't.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward have cast their net far and wide to find new players for Liverpool to target.

During the 2026-27 summer transfer window, over £150 million + was spent on upcoming players to try and bolster the Reds' ranks.

And, while some of them moves have worked out well, others haven't.

This inconsistency among Liverpool's ranks has massively impacted the way that things have gone for them this season.

Right now, they're fourth in the Premier League table but, if they want to get back to the top and start challenging for silverware, they're going to have to spend even more money.

So, that's why many newly introduced players seem to be getting linked with Liverpool all the time.

Liverpool and Manchester City want to sign Yunus Akgun.

One area that Liverpool heavily focused on improving in the summer was their attack.

Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz were signed in the summer transfer window just gone and, the season before that, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Florian Wirtz were all brought in.

And, while all of these additions looked good on paper, some of them just haven't kicked on with Liverpool still needing to add some newly introduced faces to their ranks.

Many different players have been presented as options to Liverpool over the last couple of months but now, thanks to an upgrade from X account Mekteb-i Gala (who have over 50,000 followers), Galatasaray attacker Yunus Akgun is now on Liverpool's radar.

"EXCLUSIVE | PSG, Manchester City, Liverpool, Atletico Madrid, Como and Juventus are monitoring Yunus Akgün in every match," they wrote.

"They are in the process of gathering information on the player.".

Yunus Akgun could be a cheap option for Liverpool to explore.

Since Yunus Akgun is 26 years old, he's a tad older than most of the Reds' recent targets.

A lot of Liverpool's transfer plans over the last couple of years have consisted of signing young players for the future.

This has been proven by the recent arrivals of Munoz, Barcola and Wirtz.

And, while all of these players are good enough to feature in Liverpool's starting XI now, the fact that they have potential to become even better is extremely exciting.

Indeed, Akgun isn't at the end of his career yet but, after he contributed to 21 goals last season and has already scored four goals this term, it's unclear if he's already reached his peak or not.

The fact that he can be used as a left-winger or a number 10 is also another major selling point of the attacker.

No fee was mentioned for Akgun but, of all the players who have surfaced as potential options recently, the Turkiye international who's appeared 25 times for his country, looks like one of the most exciting.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luciano Spalletti revealed youngster Jeff Ekhator will feature in Juventus' Europa League clash with Omonia Nicosia as they hope to have "an extra solution moving forward".

Ekhator joined Juve from Genoa in the summer, but missed the start of the season through injury.

The 20-year-old made his competitive debut off the bench in Juve's Europa League win over AZ, while he also made a substitute appearance in their Serie A draw with Fiorentina before the international break.

Ekhator, who scored for Italy's Under-21s during that break, was an unused substitute against Venezia last weekend, but will play on Thursday as Spalletti looks to add another attacking option alongside Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade.

Recent findings suggest that "We have a lot of top-quality players, and they're all good. We also need to develop some young players," noted Spalletti.

Industry observers note that "We'll play Ekhator because we want an extra solution moving forwards. We will make rotations that we trust in. We're aware of what is at stake.

It has been revealed that "[Italy U21 boss Silvio] Baldini speaks very highly of him, and Baldini is one of my close friends within football. I'm getting to know him a bit better now, and I agree with Baldini.

"I expect him to be calm, but he's a player with good prospects, and all great players started out as a talent with good prospects before reaching that level.".

Juve have won all four of their previous European meetings with Omonia, beating them twice in the 1977-78 European Cup and twice in the 1999-00 UEFA Cup. They also have a 100% win ratio against Cypriot sides, winning seven out of seven games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that Markus Krösche will soon get to work at AC Milan, but Gerry Cardinale will remain involved.

It has not been a very well-kept secret that Milan have been pushing for the arrival of Krösche since the summer, when it looked as though the German director was all set to arrive alongside Ruben Amorim, before Eintracht Frankfurt put up a wall.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Rather than turn to an alternative appointment, the Rossoneri decided to internally promote some figures while leaving the vacancy open. Ultimately they were waiting for developments on Krösche, and he officially left the Bundesliga side last month, leaving him available to finally join.

Industry observers note that on Monday, there was talk of a release clause paid to Eintracht. In a video published on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano revealed some added information about Krösche’s imminent arrival and what it will mean regarding Cardinale’s involvement.

Industry observers note that “Confirmation has arrived, and I would say finally, also from Germany of something we have been telling you for weeks: Markus Krosche will be the new Head of Football at Milan. In Germany there has been a much slower narrative, much more, let’s say, Eintracht-centric,” he said (via MilanNews).

According to recent reports, “The reality is that Milan has had an agreement with Krosche for some time, Milan also has everything ready for the official announcement which is expected shortly. Milan will not pay 5 million, but 4 million euros in compensation to Eintracht Frankfurt to free Krosche, who already said goodbye to the German club some time ago.

“He will be ready and operational from the beginning of December to work on the winter transfer market with Gerry Cardinale, Ruben Amorim and the entire work group that is dealing with Milan. So there were never any doubts whatsoever.

“Markus Krosche is ready to take control of the Rossoneri mercato with Gerry Cardinale, who will be absolutely present, a key player, and involved. After Milan’s excellent victory against Frosinone, the Milan owner reiterated that if Milan competes for a player, it will be to win, not to participate. In short, this is another sign of Milan’s ambition.”.

Chelsea should sign Virgil van Dijk as a free agent if he decides against extending his Liverpool contract, Jamie Redknapp believes.

Xabi Alonso already has a lengthy to-do list as he looks to get Chelsea on song, but patching a leaky back line is a top priority. They have already shipped 20 goals in the league this season and have only kept two league clean sheets in their last 27 matches.

A fine market opportunity could arise in the summer as they look to bolster their ranks, though, as Liverpool captain Van Dijk could become a free agent.

Recent findings suggest that the Dutchman is into the final year of his contract and, at 35 years of age, remains one of the game’s finest centre-backs. It remains to be seen whether he will extend his Liverpool deal, though, as he noted earlier this month: “I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion. Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.”.

For Redknapp, Chelsea would be foolish not to make a move for Van Dijk, who he believes could emulate Thiago Silva’s impact on the club.

“All the great centre-back partnerships, you always have one that’s the dominant one, and normally one that will maybe drop off,” he explained.

Recent findings suggest that “If you talk about probably as good as anything, say Virgil [van Dijk] and Jacquet at the moment, you wouldn’t even know who’s who. They’re both aggressive and they go and win challenges.”.

Redknapp, speaking on The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Vegas, continued: “But I’ve seen Chelsea’s defence get bullied time after time. Brian Brobbey was obviously one a few weeks ago at Sunderland. And again, Dominic Calvert-Lewin. They cannot live with anyone that’s got any physicality.

Industry observers note that “[Levi] Colwill is what you would call, in our day, a number two centre-back, which would be the one that would maybe sweep up behind. [Wesley] Fofana, the same. They haven’t got that player.

“Do they need to just go and, as I keep hearing people say, ‘You need to buy a centre-back.’”.

Redknapp, who spent 11 years at Liverpool as a player, continued, saying Van Dijk could be exactly what Chelsea need to bolster their defence, but he started with the caveat: “I don’t know for sure, he might end up staying. I hope he does. (Chelsea) should try and get Virgil van Dijk in the summer. That’s what I’d do.

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

Lewis Potter starred at left-back, registering seven shots — the most of any player — and the joint-most touches in the opposition box. He was a menace and integral to every Brentford attack.

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

Industry observers note that it will split opinion, but in this day and age it is a clear red card. Although the Everton defender won the ball, his studs connected with Yehor Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through.

The speed and intensity of the tackle endangered his opponent. He had to go.

In a recent development, referee Craig Pawson brandished a yellow, but a quick trip to the monitor saw it upgraded. Tarkowski ran down the tunnel before Pawson could even get the red card out of his pocket.

The home support enjoyed it, having taunted their former player throughout the first half.

To compound Everton’s misery, the first game of Tarkowski three-match ban is next weekend’s Merseyside derby.

Although Tarkowski won the ball, his studs connected with Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through.

A deflated Moyes had few complaints. ‘My feeling at the time was it wasn’t a red because James easily got to the ball before the Brentford player,’ the Everton boss stated.

‘But after I saw it again, Tarky's boot is a bit higher than I'd like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.

According to recent reports, ‘We didn’t play well. Brentford did and credit to them. A bit unfortunate with the goals, it made it look even worse than it was.’.

Everton were unbeaten in four games at Brentford before this and their defeat came in the form of the sublime and the ridiculous.

The first goal was all about Anthony undoing Everton on the left before Lewis-Potter was given far too much space to get his shot away. The deflection was unfortunate, but the defending was poor to begin with.

Tarkowski blocked an initial effort from Lewis-Potter for the second goal but the ball fell straight back to him, and Jake O’Brien helped his second attempt past Jordan Pickford. Once again, Everton should have done better and cleared the initial free-kick.

Portuguese forward Fabio Carvalho could not believe his luck when he added a late fourth, tapping in as Mathias Jensen’s corner flew straight past the congested pack at the near post.

Liverpool have successfully negotiated the option to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye once he turns 18.

Ndiaye, at the moment 16, trialled with Liverpool’s academy in the summer of 2025 and now has a clear pathway to Merseyside.

Per reports from The Athletic, the Reds have pipped a number of European rivals to get right of first refusal for his signing in January 2028.

English clubs cannot sign players from overseas until they have turned 18, which Ndiaye will do on New Year’s Eve in 2027.

Ndiaye right now plies his trade in his home nation with Diambars FC, whom he helped earn promotion to the Senegalese top flight last season.

Ndiaye is currently away at the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, picking up a goal and two assists in a 9-0 drubbing of Cuba earlier this week.

It has been revealed that senegal’s only other match at the tournament so far resulted in a 1-1 draw with Croatia. Liverpool fans hoping to get a glimpse of a future star, though, might be tempted to tune into their meeting with Tajikistan on Thursday, November 26.

Sources indicate that liverpool have made a habit of spotting talent at such tournaments. At last year’s U17 World Cup, their scouts brought home Senegal’s Mor Talla Ndiaye, Austria’s Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Belgium’s Lucca Brughmans.

It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will opt to sign Ndiaye in 2028, and what role he might play at the club if they do.

Ndiaye will hope to follow in the footsteps of one of Liverpool’s all-time greats, his countryman Sadio Mane, in making the move to the north-west.

New head coach Mauricio Pochettino endured a horror start to his Man Utd tenure with a heavy 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

And he unsurprisingly does not keep his place in Lisbon, with Harry Maguire restored.

Diogo Dalot failed to impress on Sunday and sees himself rotated out for Noussair Mazraoui, while in the engine room, Youri Tielemans was hooked for Mason Mount in the second half. The Belgian keeps his place.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has noted that his future is right now "not vital".

Fernandes, 32, only has a contract with the Red Devils until the end of the campaign, but the club do have the option to extend it for a further 12 months.

The Portugal international has reportedly rejected Man United's latest offer, allegedly wanting a longer deal with higher wages given his contribution during a tough period.

There is at the moment speculation surrounding his future at Old Trafford, but Fernandes has insisted that his main focus for the moment is on helping Man United to turn their campaign around.

"For us to start winning games and then we can talk about contract," Fernandes told reporters ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, when asked what would need to happen for him to sign a latest deal.

"It’s not key now. It’s my future, I haven’t got much left in my contract, but we will have time to speak about that. The conversations stopped when we thought now was not the moment.".

Fernandes also refused to "close the door" on returning to Sporting before the end of his career.

According to recent reports, "I will never close the door to [returning to] Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart," the Man United captain added.

The Portuguese represented Sporting between 2017 and 2020 ahead of a move to Man United, scoring 63 goals and registering 50 assists in 137 appearances for the club.

Since arriving at Man United, Fernandes has a record of 113 goals and 111 assists in 342 appearances for the English team in all competitions.

Fernandes is again expected to be in the starting side when the Red Devils tackle Sporting in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

The playmaker has six goals and three assists in 15 appearances in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Fernandes has a record of nine goals and 12 assists in 29 career appearances in the Champions League during his time at Sporting and Man United.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Former Portugal head coach Roberto Martinez said it was a "pleasure" to coach Cristiano Ronaldo, who he believes is on the same level as Diego Maradona, Johan Cruyff and Lionel Messi.

Ronaldo confirmed his international retirement just days before the most recent break, bringing down the curtain on a glittering career with Portugal.

He is the leading scorer and appearance-maker in the history of men's internationals, plundering 146 goals in 234 games since his Portugal debut in 2003.

His Portugal career ended on a bit of a dour note, as he left the September-October camp early after a falling-out with upcoming boss Jorge Jesus, which resulted in him being handed a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF).

During Martinez's tenure, he led Portugal to the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 and won the 2024-25 Nations League but stepped down after their last-16 exit to eventual champions Spain at this year's World Cup.

The Spaniard highlighted just how significant a mark Ronaldo made on Portugal's history and had high praise for his former captain.

"For me, it was a pleasure," Martinez said on Amazon Prime when asked about Ronaldo.

Sources indicate that "For me and my technical staff, it was a joy to work with him for 37 games. He scored 28 goals [in 37 games under Martinez], and that's probably one of the iconic figures.

"I don't think we will see a player of that stature [again] in Portugal.

"In the last few days, you've had so many subjective opinions about what the player is now, [but] what is not subjective are the stats.

Industry observers note that "The way he has impacted the game. We are talking about a player that maybe [is of the level of] Lionel Messi, [Diego] Maradona, Johan Cruyff; those are the stats that a player like Cristiano [has].".

Portugal estará sempre em mim https://t.co/dnFj51rxmh.

— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026.

Ronaldo retires as the only player to have scored at least 10 goals at both the World Cup (11) and the European Championships (14), with the latter figure being a competition record.

He became the first player to score in six different editions of the World Cup this year, when he helped himself to a brace in a group-stage win over Uzbekistan, and he is also the oldest player to feature in a World Cup knockout-stage match, at the age of 41.

"I don't think you can [surpass his numbers]," Martinez added.

"It's something that you learn with Cristiano; his mindset is not winning something or his motivation wasn't to win the Ballon d'Or.

Recent findings suggest that "His motivation was to be better the next day. His commitment to the game is second to none, and I think the longevity is above any opinion.

"Portugal has a population of 10 million. When Cristiano Ronaldo arrives to the national team [in 2003], [Portugal in] 23-and-a-half seasons have never missed a major tournament.

"That's down to what he brought: the professionalism and his numbers – 234 games [for the national team].".

The Red Devils’ new boss is facing just his second match in charge of the club as he looks to bounce back from the weekend’s chastening 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

He will return to the Champions League for the first time since leaving Paris Saint-Germain this evening, with a tricky tie away at Sporting on the docket.

However, in a selection blow, he will not be able to make use of one of his more threatening forwards, with Cunha left out of the Lisbon-bound travelling squad.

There was some positive news in the squad, though, as Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow came back into contention after injury layoffs, but the absence of Cunha is a serious setback for Pochettino as he looks to breathe life into his nascent United tenure.

Matheus Cunha was left out of the travelling squad for Manchester United’s meeting with Sporting as he is serving a red card suspension.

The Brazilian forward was dismissed in second-half injury time as United came from behind to beat Roma 3-2 last time out in the Champions League.

Having trailed by two goals to nil with just 17 minutes played, a second-half penalty from Bruno Fernandes and a quickfire brace from Cunha flipped the script.

Cunha, though, was shown two yellow cards in a chaotic finish.

The first came when he removed his shirt celebrating what proved to be the winning goal, and he picked up a second in the 91st minute for a needless, reckless late tackle on Leonardo Balerdi.

Cunha is only suspended for one match.

He will serve his suspension against Sporting tonight and be available again when United host RB Leipzig in two weeks’ time, on December 8.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:31.

Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

Mauricio Pochettino will now take charge of his first European match for Man United, and there is pressure on the Argentine following the four-goal mauling at Anfield.

When asked whether the Sporting match provided Man United with the perfect chance to bounce back from the defeat to Liverpool, Strachan insisted that the players need to show character and heart in a bid to turn the club's campaign around.

According to recent reports, "Well, to be fair, Liverpool should never really be a massive ask for Man United as such, because the record there is terrific over the years. I mean, it's always been decent. That fixture is one of the ones that Liverpool really want to win because they know how dangerous Man United are," said Strachan.

In a recent development, "But it wasn't a real game after the first two goals, there was the sending-off, you know. And even the free kick, you think, right, if you see the free kick off, we can reorganise and organise with 10 players. We never even had time to do that. So, as a manager, you can't count that, you've just got to count that as a no-game.

It has been revealed that "But what you can do in that situation is ask, who kept pressing? Who do I want in my team? Because in adversity, you see the real character coming out, and in adversity in big games, you see the real character. And it's not on your social media, it's not saying to the fans, we love you and we're sorry and all the rest of it. Don't apologise to me, just do something about it.

It has been revealed that "Don't come in and hold your hand up and say, I'm sorry, gaffer. Don't apologise to me because I'm not interested in you telling me you're sorry for making a mistake. Just don't make a mistake. And if you do make a mistake, rectify it as quickly as possible.

"What I'm talking about is managers will try and sort it out. Invariably, unless you can do something about it, physically or mentally, then it will appear again. They will appear, and they'll appear in crisis moments.

"As I mentioned, your character is shown up in crisis times and the same mistakes will be made by the same people whoever they play. And some people are just not good enough to play at this level.

In a recent development, "You know, we all talk about shapes and systems and this and that. The funny thing is, I don't think there's too many people talking about systems now. I think most people are now talking about, even if you talk with a bright manager, they talk about putting people under pressure, winning knockdowns, getting to the ball first, getting the ball to your front men.

According to recent reports, "So, the system thing has kind of changed now. The only one that kind of really changes, it's gone from a back four to a back three, but the rest, like Brighton, Liverpool, Bournemouth, they're all playing the same sort of way.

"It's a kind of 4-2-3-1, where the four players up front are attacking players, whatever way you want to use it, two wide men, just off the front. Wales were the same with Craig Bellamy.

Industry observers note that "So, I think that people are moving to that in general now, but there's not too much talking about systems now. It's more about closing down, getting to knockdowns, winning headers and free kicks and corner kicks.".

Man United have six points to show from their two matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

Mauricio Pochettino has explained his decision to hand Joshua Zirkzee a first start of the season against Sporting in the Champions League.

The Argentine named just his second United team in Lisbon on Wednesday evening as he looked to bounce back from a damning 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on his managerial bow.

In Portugal, he made four changes from the side he named at Anfield, with Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui and Amad Diallo all coming into the side.

Perhaps his most notable call, though, saw striker Zirkzee chosen to lead the line, making his first start of the campaign.

The Dutchman has been bumped up the pecking order somewhat for this match, with fellow striker Benjamin Sesko out injured and deputy Matheus Cunha suspended.

Pochettino, though, said he hopes Zirkzee can kick on as a more dependable option, given United’s thin ranks.

Industry observers note that asked to explain the selection, he told TNT Sports: “Cunha is suspended, of course, Sesko is injured. I think it is a great opportunity for Josh (Zirkzee) to show his quality.

“I think it is an important game to start to think that he can be a very important player for the team, and today is an opportunity for him.”.

It has been revealed that zirkzee was entirely peripheral under Michael Carrick and had looked to leave United in the summer transfer window. He was the subject of a loan bid from Everton on Deadline Day, but no move materialised.

Pochettino, though, seems optimistic he can bring Zirkzee in from the cold as United look to salvage their campaign, both domestically and abroad.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly revealed his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'.

Romelu Lukaku revealed his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.

In a recent development, former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal.

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan stated.

In a recent development, 'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

In a recent development, 'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'.

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his intends, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

'16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

Sources indicate that 'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

Andoni Iraola finally seems to be turning things around at Liverpool.

His squad are just coming off the back of a 4-0 win against arch-rivals Manchester United which proved how good they can be.

Indeed, the Red Devils did end up with a red card within the first 10 minutes of the clash but, the football that Liverpool played on Sunday was some of their best of the season.

If they continue performing like that, there's a good chance that they could get themselves back into the race for the Premier League title.

At the moment, seven points separate them and first-placed Arsenal and, while that's still quite a major gap, it's a number that they can start hacking away at fairly easily.

This task would be made an awful lot easier if, during the January transfer window, Liverpool manage to add one or two new faces to their ranks.

Liverpool have been 'in contact' with Lamine Camara.

Lamine Camara is one of the main players who was linked with Liverpool in the summer.

The Senegalese midfielder was rumoured to be one of the Reds' priority targets with them, alongside many other clubs vying for his transfer, despite his €70 million price tag.

Liverpool were the first ones to be linked with the 22-year-old but, when all the other clubs entered the race, the deal got too messy and in the end, they pulled out.

However, there were some rumours on transfer deadline day which claimed that Liverpool had told AS Monaco and Camara to wait for them until January.

And, to the surprise of many, they did just that and pulled out of their deal with Chelsea at the last minute.

The ending of negotiations led to many different questions being asked and several rumours being shared but now, David Lynch, while speaking to Anfield Index, has confirmed that "contact" has been held between the two parties.

"Liverpool did have a word with his representatives and just remarked kind of hang on for us," he said.

"I’ve got much more solid information that he’s someone that they really like.

"[He is] a player that they like that they’ve been in contact with.".

Liverpool must decide who they want their next central midfielder to be.

As of now, nobody knows exactly what Liverpool's intends for the January transfer window are.

Many different rumours have been shared with fans, pundits and journalists all making up their own theories.

But, only those within the Reds' recruitment department will know exactly what lies ahead.

However, if their intends don't include a fresh central midfielder, some serious questions will need to be asked.

Many different players have emerged as options for Liverpool, and, if a upcoming one is on their shortlist, they need to figure out who it's going to be.

Whether it's Camara, Scott, Wharton or even an out there option like Gavi, a decision needs to be made rapidly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Freddie Cotton | 24 Nov 2026 20:48, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:58.

Marseille welcome Levski Sofia to the Stade Velodrome on Thursday evening on matchday five of the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Les Olympiens claimed a crucial 1-0 win away to Bayer Leverkusen, while the Blues beat Polish side Jagiellonia by the same scoreline at the National Stadium Vasil Levski.

After narrowly missing out on booking their place in the UEFA Champions League for the second consecutive year last season, finishing fifth in Ligue 1 and just one point below Lyon in fourth, Marseille will be extremely disappointed with how they have performed on the continent so far this campaign.

Although they edged out Leverkusen in their latest Europa League fixture, losses to Sturm Graz, Olympiacos and Besiktas in each of their opening three matches mean Bruno Genesio’s men have earned just three points so far in Europe, leaving them 31st in the league phase table and outside of the knockout stage places.

Despite conceding two late goals to lose against Le Mans on Sunday evening, Les Olympiens have seen a huge improvement in their league endeavours, having won each of their prior five matches to at the moment sit fifth in the Ligue 1 table and just three points outside the automatic Champions League qualification places.

Marseille are yet to claim victory over Levski, though they do boast a mainly positive record against Bulgarian opposition, having beaten CSKA Sofia in each of their other two meetings with efbet League sides.

Having won their first efbet League title since 2009 last season and finished 10 points ahead of runners-up Ludogorets, who had triumphed in each of the previous 14 consecutive campaigns, Levski competed in the qualifying stages of the Champions League for the first time in 17 years during the summer.

The Blues impressed in their efforts for tournament qualification, beating Borac Banja Luka, Univ Craiova and Kairat Almaty to progress to the decisive playoff tie, but having endured a 4-0 aggregate defeat against Greek giants AEK Athens, the Bulgarian side are instead competing in the Europa League this season.

However, Julio Velazquez’s men have given a good account of themselves so far on the continent as after taking just one point from their first two matches, Levski have won back-to-back matches in the Europa League to sit 10th in the standings with seven points and only outside the round-of-16 positions on goal difference.

While the Blues do not have the best recent record against French opposition, having won just one of their previous four meetings with Ligue 1 sides, that triumph did come over Marseille, with Levski securing a 1-0 win over Les Olympiens in the group stages of this competition in December 2005, when it was branded as the UEFA Cup.

On a more positive note, after missing the match against Leverkusen as a precaution, Moroccan forward Amine Harit has started Les Olympiens’ previous two league fixtures and looks set to return to feature from the off in the week too.

Netting eight Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous four outings, Algerian forward Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly the hosts’ biggest threat going forward and will be hoping to add to his winner against Leverkusen last time out in the competition.

Having been left out of Levski’s Europa League squad list, Oliver Kamdem, Mustapha Sangare and Petko Hristov are all unavailable for Thursday’s fixture, while 34-year-old striker Radoslav Kirilov remains out with a knee glitch.

However, the Blues will be delighted to have welcomed midfielder Asen Mitkov back from injury against Lok. Sofia on Sunday afternoon and the 21-year-old will be hopeful for more minutes in the week too.

Contributing to six goals in 12 league appearances, Portuguese midfielder Serginho has been the visitors’ dangerman so far this season and will be hoping to replicate his efbet League form on the continent this week.

Having finally bounced back from their three-game losing streak in the Europa League by claiming an crucial win over Leverkusen in their latest European outing, Marseille will certainly be aiming to fight their way into the knockout progression places with victory on Thursday evening.

While Levski have made a promising start to their campaign, we think Les Olympiens will bag all three points at the Stade Velodrome this week and are backing them to mount a late charge for a top-eight finish in the league phase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Isak is closing in on a record held by Mohamed Salah with his latest Liverpool goal.

The Swedish striker did not take long to open the scoring as Liverpool faced Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Bradley Barcola won the ball high up the pitch to set the Reds on the attack and Dominik Szoboszlai teed Isak up to finish from close range.

It was a significant goal for Isak, who has now scored in six consecutive away matches for Liverpool.

It is a feat that very few men have bettered. According to the stat gurus at Opta, no Liverpool player has ever scored in more than seven consecutive away appearances.

Sources indicate that salah is the current record holder, and should Isak find the back of the net in this weekend’s Merseyside derby at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he would equal the Egyptian king’s record. Add another against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on December 5, and he could surpass it.

Prior to the launch of the Premier League, Sam English, John Evans and John Aldridge all scored in seven consecutive away matches.

Salah called time on his Liverpool career at the end of last season, leaving with 257 goals and 123 assists across 442 appearances.

He now plies his trade in Turkey with Trabzonspor, where he has made a bright start to life, tallying 16 goal contributions in his first 17 appearances.

Liverpool have been hit with a major injury blow as Victor Munoz was forced off in the first half of their Champions League meeting with Club Brugge.

The young Spaniard threw himself into an aggressive challenge on Jorne Spileers shortly before half-time - but came off far worse after appearing to knock knees with the Belgian.

Munoz looked to be in considerable pain as he stayed down and Liverpool’s medical staff were waved onto the pitch. There was a lengthy delay as he received treatment.

He was surrounded by concerned-looking team-mates as a stretcher was brought on to carry him off, but it was waved away and Munoz was able to leave the pitch under his own steam.

The fact he was able to do so suggests his injury may not be too severe, though Munoz still appeared to be in serious discomfort as he made his way to the bench with a pronounced limp.

Rio Ngumoha was brought on in his place, and Andoni Iraola will problem an upgrade on his condition at full-time.

Liverpool were one to the good when Munoz left the pitch, after Dominik Szoboszlai teed Alexander Isak up to score from the edge of the six-yard box with 13 minutes on the clock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 21:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:12.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has refused to confirm whether Luke Shaw will be involved in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has made the trip to Portugal alongside his teammates, having recovered from the muscular problem that has sidelined him since the early stages of October.

The 31-year-old has been a huge miss at the back for Man United, and Pochettino has welcomed the Englishman's return to fitness.

However, it remains to be seen whether he is involved against Sporting.

“All the players need to feel they can have an impact for the team and they can perform," Pochettino told reporters during his pre-game press conference.

“It’s up to us to give the opportunities to every single player in the moment that we believe that they deserve to be involved in the game.

Recent findings suggest that “Of course, I know Luke from the past, in our time in Southampton, but all [of us who are] involved, we are not the same people now. It’s more than 10 years ago.

“Obviously, it’s good to see him and he came from a small issue but now he needs to recover his best form.

“It’s good to have him, because he’s experienced everything with the squad, but we’ll see if he can be involved tomorrow or not, from the beginning or during the game.”.

Matheus Cunha is suspended for the match following his red card against Roma in the team's last European fixture, while Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are all injured for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino also insisted during his press conference that Man United are 'not a fragile team' despite their huge difficulties this season.

The Red Devils will enter the game with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, and they at the moment sit down in 19th spot in the Premier League table.

"We are not fragile, we are a strong team who last season finished third. Sometimes things happen in football for different reasons. We need to identify why and we are working on it. I think we are going to turn the situation around," said the head coach.

Man United have two wins and two draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League, beating Sabah and Roma either side of defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Tech giant, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.
  • Sources indicate that in Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame.
  • Sources indicate that stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that quickly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Tech giant, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

Sources indicate that in Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame. He was 47 years old when he landed the role of a lifetime in the legendary science fiction series Star Trek: Playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," he stepped into the shoes of the legendary Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner.

Sources indicate that stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that quickly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe. He returned to the role decades later in the spin-off series "Star Trek: Picard," which ended in 2023, proving the character's enduring appeal.

In a recent development, as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, he led the crew of the starship Enterprise, a spaceship with the sizeable mission: "To explore strange new worlds. To seek out new life and new civilizations" — and most importantly, "to boldly go where no man has gone before!".

Stewart's interest in acting was sparked in the early 1950s when a teacher asked him to recite a work by Shakespeare. His passion for Shakespeare stayed with him until the end.

Industry observers note that his parents were far removed from the glamor of the theatrical world. His father was a highly respected officer in the British Army during World War II, but at home, he was an abusive husband, and young Patrick had to helplessly witness repeated violence against his mother. Stewart wrote about his experiences with domestic violence in The Guardian in 2009. The stage, he confessed there, seemed to him "a far safer place" than reality; he saw acting as a way to escape his home life.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick began acting at the age of 12. At 16, he left school early and, thanks to a scholarship, studied acting in Bristol, England. Along the way, he worked as a journalist. In 1965, he became an official member of the Royal Shakespeare Company, and remained with the theather company from 1966 to 1982. Such was his passion for the great English playwright and lyricist that he even shared his sonnets on his Twitter account during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

It has been revealed that stewart dazzled the theater world with his own stage adaptation of Charles Dickens' 1843 tale "A Christmas Carol." He played more than 30 roles himself. After its 1987 premiere in Stewart's hometown of Mirfield, the one-man show became a critics' favorite and a long-running hit on Broadway in New York.

In the same year,  Stewart went from being a stage actor to an international TV star. Star Trek producer Robert Justman offered him the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, one of the main characters in a upcoming edition of the popular TV series "Star Trek: The Next Generation.".

The successful Shakespearean hesitated. Until then, he had never worked in Hollywood. But his agent encouraged him to accept the role, Stewart recalled in a 2020 interview with the German newspaper Die Welt. "You can accept the offer as a start for now. It won't be a substantial deal, you can't revive a series as iconic as Star Trek anyway.".

According to recent reports, but his agent was to be proven wrong: Stewart led the Starship Enterprise through its galactic adventures for seven seasons and four full-length feature films. The TV series had astronomical success on Earth in a very short time. At first, the producers were at odds as to whether Stewart's British accent could really fit the role of commander of a US starship in the 24th century, but it soon became impossible to imagine the series without the subtly diplomatic Captain Picard, who often quoted Shakespeare while at the helm. It seemed as if all the time he had spent as a Shakespearean actor had prepared him to command the Enterprise, Stewart once remarked with a wink. When the cult series ended in 1994, he had ruled out ever returning to the Enterprise's command center.

Sources indicate that in 2010, the actor was knighted by the Queen of England. Stewart considered it the greatest honor of his career to stand alongside acting greats such as Sir Laurence Olivier and Sir Alec Guinness.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the screen, Stewart has long used his voice for social and human rights causes. In recent years, he has drawn attention to problems such as violence against women, age discrimination and the protection of children.

Sources indicate that in a June 2020 interview, "Playboy" asked the Upcoming York resident whether he was considering retiring from acting. "Never! That would mean giving up my life," replied Stewart, who was approaching his 80th birthday at the time. He was filming the second of three seasons of "Star Trek: Picard." The series ends with a final episode in which the retired Starfleet admiral makes his last appearance. In the series, Picard retires to his family vineyard in France but is drawn back into space to confront new threats to the Federation.

In a recent development, this series also showcases Stewart's affection for his pit bull, Ginger. In "Star Trek: Picard," Picard also has a pit bull, a loyal four-legged companion named Number One — a deliberate reference to Stewart's real-life love of the breed. For his efforts to combat prejudice against pit bulls and to support their adoption, Stewart was honored by the US animal welfare organization ASPCA, among others.

In 2024, he published his memoir "Making it So." In it, he recounts his passion for theater and his love of Shakespeare.

Now, at the age of 86, the British actor has finally departed for another galaxy. Farewell, Patrick Stewart!

#106304. Breaking: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1179 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1179 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

The dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

Recent findings suggest that the plate and the photos are on show at the new exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, says exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Recent findings suggest that alongside Picasso, a surprising number of crucial artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Sources indicate that two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to concern a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

It has been revealed that still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

Sources indicate that however, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

The dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked substantial and dangerous.".

Industry observers note that the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian indicates. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a fresh image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

Industry observers note that the designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

Still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

But altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

Industry observers note that the feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

In a recent development, "It's really crazy," she notes, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 22:55.
  • Unai Emery has suggested that Alejandro Garnacho is far away from a first start for Aston Villa.
  • On Tuesday night, the Premier League outfit succumbed to a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Galatasaray in the Champions League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 22:55.

Unai Emery has suggested that Alejandro Garnacho is far away from a first start for Aston Villa.

On Tuesday night, the Premier League outfit succumbed to a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Galatasaray in the Champions League.

Not only are Villa now outsiders to finish in the top eight of the league phase, they have now gone six matches without a win in all competitions.

When quizzed on the prolonged wait for Garnacho to make his first Villa start, Emery has often been encouraging towards the Chelsea loanee.

However, when asked about his absence from the squad in Turkey, Emery hinted that the winger is not in his plans.

Emery named 11 substitutes - with two goalkeepers - for the Galatasaray game, one fewer than he was permitted.

Questioned over Garnacho not being involved, he told reporters: "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us.".

At his pre-match press conference, Emery stated that everyone was available, apart from Matty Cash, Matteo Ruggeri, Amadou Onana and the ineligible Brian Madjo.

Emery has been facing suggestions that Garnacho has been discarded from his aims in the same fashion as Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott in 2025-26 since September.

He seemingly spoke sincerely when saying that Garnacho had made a positive impact during training and a friendly during the September international break.

It has been revealed that however, he remains with just 64 minutes across four substitute appearances since September 5. Although the appearances required for a permanent transfer from Chelsea has never been confirmed, the assumption is that it is 10 matches.

Garnacho is on seven outings, and there is now little to no realistic prospect of Emery choosing to activate a clause that would require Villa to pay approximately £43m for his signature.

As much as Villa's hierarchy and fans back Emery, questions need to be asked how two loanees who are known to have buy clauses in their respective agreements have been frozen out so quickly.

Villa have agreed separate deals worth a combined total of £78m. Elliott and Garnacho have made just three starts - all for Elliott - between them.

One of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move as a potential successor to Alisson is Bart Verbruggen, who has been a standout at Brighton this season.

#106298. Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

📅 23 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1049 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1049 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.
  • Recent findings suggest that "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW.
  • According to recent reports, the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

Recent findings suggest that "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it.".

According to recent reports, the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

"A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity.".

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

But a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, highlights how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

Recent findings suggest that names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer mentioned their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages.".

Recent findings suggest that research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

According to recent reports, "Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

According to recent reports, even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on.".

Industry observers note that pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

"People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'".

Later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she mentioned.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

Tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to.".

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions.".

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'".

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point.".

But the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

"I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there.".

Industry observers note that but Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum noted.

Tiny describes a similar ambivalence.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it.".

In a recent development, that does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

Online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered.".

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

Pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 24 Nov 2026 23:33.

In a matchup featuring two of Ligue 1's biggest surprise stories at the moment, Brest will welcome Paris FC to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Friday.

A 1-0 win at Strasbourg on matchday 11 lifted the Brittany side to sixth in the Ligue 1 table, five points behind Paris, who are second after a convincing 4-0 triumph over Angers.

It appears as though Julien Lachuer has finally figured out the right buttons to push to help Brest find some consistency domestically.

This team entered November having dropped points in four of their last five league fixtures, but they will boast a 100% record this month should they triumph on Friday.

Brest can also win at least four domestic affairs in a row for the first time in a single league season since 2023-24 when they claimed six consecutive victories in this competition.

With a win on matchday 12, they would temporarily move into third place in Ligue 1 and that final Champions League spot above Lille on goal difference.

A team that gave up at least one goal in each of their first eight matches in this competition have not conceded in their last three such games.

After 11 matchdays, Les Pirates are third in Ligue 1 regarding expected goals but also rank third in significant chances missed (23).

Liam Rosenior must be happy to be back in France, managing in a league where he has found tremendous success as a head coach.

The man who guided Strasbourg to a place in the Conference League has transformed Paris FC into title contenders, with his side just three points below Paris Saint-Germain heading into this match.

A victory by three or more goals on Friday would temporarily put them in first place and extend their winning run in this competition to four matches.

Right now, Paris FC are averaging 2.09 points per match in this competition, which is 0.80 more than a season ago, the biggest such increase among Ligue 1 clubs over that span.

They boast the lowest expected goals conceded in the league (10.2) and are one of three teams in the top flight that have not allowed a set-piece goal so far, with PSG and Lens being the others.

Paris FC can earn a third successive Ligue 1 triumph versus Brest on Friday, beating them 2-1 in their last visit to Stade Francis-Le Ble a season ago.

A calf strain may keep Brendan Chardonnet out of the Brest fold on Friday, while Kenny Lala is questionable with a knock and Kamory Doumbia is also doubtful with an ankle injury.

Noah Edjouma netted his third of the competition last week, while Egil Selvik stopped five shots to collect his third successive clean sheet in Ligue 1.

Meanwhile, for Paris FC, Nhoa Sangui may miss another match because of a hamstring issue which he has struggled to recover from.

Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all found the back of the net on matchday 11, with each strike coming in the second half.

Brest possible starting lineup:.

Selvik; Zogbe, Tousart, Lloris, Locko; Chotard, Magnetti; Edjouma, Nonge, Mboup; Ajorque.

Paris FC possible starting lineup:.

Trapp; Matondo, Chergui, Coppola, Otavio; Lopez, Lees-Melou; Kebbal, Zabi, Pagis; Koleosho.

While Brest are trending in the right direction, Paris FC have shown more consistency all season, and we believe their overall balance will see them collect maximum points once again.

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

Industry observers note that “I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In a recent development, in Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

At Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

In a recent development, in this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

In a recent development, so far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

When Amine Adli curled in an 84-minute free-kick with his left foot at the Vitality Stadium, it put the seal on the most extraordinary evening in Bournemouth’s history. On a brutally windy and wet night, Bournemouth trounced AC Milan 3-0.

It has been revealed that few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

Recent findings suggest that back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

In a recent development, fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

According to recent reports, now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

#106291. Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
