📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when.
  • According to recent reports, the loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal.
  • “Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, remarked of his £55m signing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that from the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

According to recent reports, the loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, remarked of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”.

It has been revealed that in Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa remarked. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”.

Recent findings suggest that some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

According to recent reports, konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has rapidly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

According to recent reports, the nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

In a recent development, thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

According to recent reports, the victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also states plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

Sources indicate that “I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

According to recent reports, “We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”.

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

On bouncing back from defeat...

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”.

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

In a recent development, “They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”.

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”.

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

Recent findings suggest that this is presently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

According to recent reports, today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

Recent findings suggest that this is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz.

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta stated: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

It has been revealed that “I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes noted: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Jude Bellingham has more than settled into his routine in Madrid, with the England star learning Spanish, integrating into his community and spending time with his girlfriend in a mansion worth a reported £5.3million ($7m) after three seasons at Real Madrid.

The 23-year-old's settled life in the Spanish capital is thought to play a significant role in Bellingham's decision to sign an improved deal with the club, with Daily Mail Sport reporting on Monday that the midfielder is set to become one of Europe's highest earners.

New terms would see Bellingham raking in around £12.5million a year after tax until 2029, and will reportedly put him on par with his team-mate Vinicius Junior, whose latest deal is thought to be worth around £500,000 per week after tax.

But beyond the money, Bellingham has been flourishing turning out for the Spanish giants – both on and off the pitch.

Here, Daily Mail Sport details Bellingham's lifestyle in Spain, and the rituals that have grounded the player after his explosion into superstardom.

Jude Bellingham is inching closer to a new deal at Real Madrid to become one of Europe's highest earners.

But more than just enjoying his football, Bellingham has made himself at home in the city (pictured at the Grand Prix of Spain in Madrid this year).

A recurring theme when Bellingham speaks of his love of living in Madrid stems from an established daily routine.

Speaking to his club just six months after he joined Los Blancos in the summer of 2023, Bellingham had already set up habits which helped him feel at home in the new city.

In a recent development, 'I get up early to go to training, I train and then I head home,' Bellingham remarked. 'Sometimes I'll go out for a coffee near home or head into town to grab something to eat. Then I go back home to chill out in the garden for a bit if the weather is good and the sun's out.

Sources indicate that 'If my friends are over, we'll go out for dinner and then back home. It's great. You get to know the people at the places you visit more often. They don't see you as Jude Bellingham the footballer, but as Jude the guy who comes in for a coffee and that's great. The people I meet in the city really look after me. I feel at home.'.

Sources indicate that over two years later, and the patterns are no different. The Calvin Klein ambassador told Vogue this month that his ideal downtime involves 'being in the tech giant of my friends and family, having a coffee, going for a walk.

'You're always going to get recognised, but you're a bit safer in terms of not getting mobbed,' Bellingham said of his favourite spots on the fringes of the city, where many of his repeat haunts are located.

It has been revealed that not that Bellingham is a little averse to integrating with the community. In fact, mingling with the locals has been a positive aspect of Bellingham's life abroad, with the player admitting in the summer of 2025 that Spain was very much 'home'.

Sources indicate that 'When I go back to play with the national team, it's nice seeing people that I don't normally get to see – my family and friends – but I always feel more comfortable when I'm back in Madrid,' Bellingham said in an interview with FIFA. 'It's the weather, the people are so loving, the food.

'You mix all that together, as well as, especially, playing for Real Madrid… When you go out in public and the people see you, you see it's like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity that they've had to meet you.

In a recent development, 'They talk to you about the club and how much it means to them. A lot of the older ladies give me kisses on the cheeks and stuff like that! It's really nice.'.

Bellingham has connected with fresh head coach Jose Mourinho since his arrival in the summer.

Shortly after his move to Madrid Bellingham moved into a villa within the upscale complex at La Finca (flats inside the community pictured).

Bellingham and his girlfriend Ashyn Castro enjoy a life of habits when together in Madrid, involving coffee walks and going out for dinner (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram).

The 23-year-old lives in his mansion with his mother Denise, who often drives him to training as he is without a license.

Shortly after moving to Spain, Bellingham settled down in the exclusive La Finca neighbourhood, which plays host to a number of his team-mates including Kylian Mbappe and former club legends such as Zinedine Zidane, Cristiano Ronaldo and Iker Casillas.

The gated community is known as 'Madrid's Beverly Hills' to insiders and boasts extensive security to ensure the luxury villas inside the compound stay safe.

Bellingham is believed to have purchased his pricey six-bedroom home in 2023, moving into the complex, which boasts a home theatre, outdoor pool and gym according to Architectural Digest, with his mother Denise.

From there, his mum drives him to and from training, with the young star admitting in Vogue that despite his prodigious footballing talent, he remains borderline incapable in other aspects of life.

'I can't cook, I can't drive… I'm good at what I do, but everything else?' he joked. 'Not that great.

'I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff – chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else. That's where I'm at. I work hard every day and all day, and then when I get home, I've probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. But there'll be a time and a place for that, I'm sure.'.

In keeping with the idea that Bellingham has found his home in Spain, it stands to reason that the player has been working on his languages.

Bellingham revealed in Vogue that he has been learning Spanish for over two years, beginning in earnest just months after his move to the Santiago Bernabeu.

Confirming his aptitude for the language, Bellingham added: 'I think a substantial part of it is being confident enough to just speak.

'You know you're going to get stuff wrong, and you're probably not going to sound exactly right, (but if) people know what you're talking about, they'll probably think: "Fair play for trying".'.

Castro and Bellingham have been dating for nearly two years since early 2025, having reportedly met on exclusive dating site Raya (Source: Ashlyn Castro/Instagram).

American model Castro is a frequent fixture in the stands whether Bellingham is playing for Madrid or England.

With Bellingham settled in Madrid, his American model girlfriend Ashlyn Castro is, if not permanently based in the city, a regular visitor to both his La Finca villa and Real Madrid's home ground.

The former music video star and Bellingham have been dating since early 2025, with Castro becoming a frequent fixture at the Bernabeu alongside his mother Denise.

Castro has also been following his exploits for England too, travelling across the United States to follow the travails of Thomas Tuchel and Co as they reached the semi-finals at this summer's World Cup.

Most recently she was spotted in the stands closer to home however, with Bellingham and Castro snapped embracing after the final whistle blew on England's impressive win against Spain at Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano.

Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Two points dropped in a game of two halves

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1390 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment.
  • A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time.
  • Sources indicate that the lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment. Arsenal were 1-0 up, well on top and absolutely deserving of the lead. Newcastle had struggled to exert any kind of control, and we’d already had 9 attempts on goal.

A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time. Unfortunately for him and for us, Lewis Hall produced a quite outstanding piece of defending to slide in and block the shot over the bar. That was the difference between Arsenal going in 2-0 up at the break rather than with just the single goal margin.

Sources indicate that the lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back. Newcastle’s only chance had come early, a shot from Jacob Murphy that deflected off his own player and drifted wide with David Raya wrong-footed. After that, we bossed the half, with 11 shots in total, 65% possession, but still only that one goal.

It feels redundant to say this is a very, very good Arsenal team, but if we have a weakness, it’s that we don’t turn this kind of domination into more goals. Very often we don’t need to as our defensive solidity and consistency keeps the opposition at bay, but last night we let our standards slip in that regard, and the lack of firepower or being clinical in the final third came home to roost.

In a recent development, it was, very literally, a game of two halves. Newcastle made a triple sub at the break and it would be churlish not to give them credit for the fact it made a positive impact. However, the Arsenal performance was night and day. The opposition upped the energy and intensity, and we made mistakes. Odegaard miskicking a Riccardo Calafiori throw-in provided them the opportunity to equalise, and I do wonder why Harvey Barnes was so free at the back post to slide home for 1-1.

In a recent development, that goal gave them momentum, they caused us problems again and again, some of them of our own making with carelessness and misfortune. Eze got back well to defend in our box but unfortunately slipped, Raya’s clearance was unconvincing and then Gabriel had to boot the ball behind for a corner – from which they made it 2-1. Dan Burn drifted off Jurrien Timber to get a free header, the ball scrambled around a bit before Malick Thiaw poked it over the line to give them the lead. Messy, shambolic defending – not very Arsenal at all.

Recent findings suggest that if we’re being fair, we have to say they could have scored again. David Raya went off with a shoulder injury, Kepa had to make a smart save at the feet of Lewis Miley but why was he one on one with the keeper in the first place? A Joe Willock shot deflected wide in similar fashion to the Murphy one in the first half, and eventually Arteta changed things with Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly coming on for Eze and Bruno Guimaraes who had a quiet return to his former club – bar that first half moment when he almost got enough contact on a fantastic Declan Rice cross but could only put the ball wide from close range.

We did get an equaliser, and very well worked it was too. We played the ball across the back line from right to left, into midfield where Havertz’s smart dummy allowed Odegaard room to drive on and find Madueke. He was Arsenal’s best attacking player last night, he kept trying to make things happen, and while I think the Newcastle keeper will probably have nightmares about letting that shot in, Madueke deserved the goal, and it earned us a point.

Recent findings suggest that it was after the 90th minute when the manager brought on Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino to try and find a winner, the Swede had one shot over the bar from the edge of the box, but had we found another, it would have been a real smash and grab. In the end, the draw was probably a fair result based on how the game played out, and afterwards the manager was unhappy at leaving two points behind:.

It has been revealed that my feeling is that we have lost two points today. And I say we because we were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. It should have been two, three or four-nil up, clear. But it wasn’t.

We started to lose duels, we started to lose second balls. We gave the ball away and have really poor circulation balls against their press and their waves. And when that happens, you give them belief.

It’s a pity because the margin should have been, again, much bigger for the level that we’ve shown.

It has been revealed that and this is the key for me. It should have been, but it wasn’t, and it too often isn’t. As I noted above, our defensive brilliance is fundamental to us winning so many games, but football is a game of variance. You can’t always control everything. On another night Odegaard just puts his foot through that throw in and that first Newcastle goal doesn’t happen. Eze and Raya deal better with that situation and we don’t concede a corner. We can focus on those individual things and say we could and should do better for sure, but you have to allow for some of that over the course of a season. You cannot be perfect for 90+ minutes 38 games in every league campaign.

The ongoing matter for me is our firepower though. I thought generally the front three played pretty well last night, and it’s not as if we missed a glut of chances, but it’s about turning the level of dominance we had in that first half into more goals. This isn’t a one-time issue either. We scored two lovely goals last night but we should have had that game firmly in our grasp at half-time, but in this league a single goal margin is never a sure thing.

The summer was a let-down in an attacking sense, there’s no getting away from that. If we had a forward line that was even close to our midfield and defence in terms of quality and depth, the Premier League would be a cakewalk. I know that’s a bit simplistic, but it’s also a fact. Regardless of what you think of the business, we let goals go to Turkey and Saudi Arabia, and replaced them with a player who has yet to score. Which isn’t to lay the blame at the feet of Tzolis, far from it, but with the squad planning/building that was undertaken.

For me, January becomes increasingly key because the improvement required is obvious, and for a sporting director whose track record looks quite hit and miss as it is, he needs a convincing window or the questions around the job he’s doing will become louder and louder, and for good reason.

The other big problem from yesterday was the injury to David Raya. It didn’t look good at all, and any absence for him would be a huge blow to the team. He’s been the best in the Premier League, and perhaps the best in Europe, for the last 18 months, and inevitably there’s a drop-off when any club is without their first choice keeper for any period of time. That’s another adjustment we’re probably going to have to make, and if it means we’re likely to be less secure and clean sheets are harder to come by, then that issue of scoring goals and being more potent comes into even sharper focus. Let’s keep fingers crossed it’s not as bad as it appears to be.

In a recent development, right, I’ll leave it there for now. There’s plenty to unpick from this one, so I’ll leave you to it in the Arses. More here tomorrow, including an Arsecast Extra. Until then, have a great Sunday.

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds revealed just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

Industry observers note that at first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

According to recent reports, for years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

It has been revealed that but in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an glitch Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Industry observers note that others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

Industry observers note that the "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Sources indicate that despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

Recent findings suggest that the eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been announced, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The new trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

It has been revealed that J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO indicates, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the fresh production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently noted she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

In a recent development, meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

“When I returned home that evening, with my parents and cousin, I burst into tears. I was overjoyed by the goal, but at the same time deeply disappointed by what had happened. It wasn’t easy at first, but I also worked on my mental health and managed to put that moment behind me.

“Today, I’m proud of the journey I’ve taken and of having overcome those difficulties.”.

“I remember what Gabbia told me: he was sorry for what happened, but he explained that the experience should give me even more motivation. It should push me to improve, to train harder, and to work so I can relive even more wonderful emotions.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that with any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them.
  • In a recent development, if Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that over the last few weeks, I’ve grown accustomed to waking up and experiencing low-level fear first thing in the morning. Today, it was a nice change not to be focused on my own health, and instead for my anxiety to centre around someone else – David Raya.

It has been revealed that with any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them. It doesn’t mean there isn’t still a kind of hierarchy, just that you’re better able to cope if injury or suspension hits. Mikel Arteta referencing ‘finishers’ rather than substitutes might be a psychological ploy to keep his squad happy, but it’s more easy to apply when you have the group of players he has at his disposal.

In a recent development, if Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White. If Riccardo Calafiori can’t play, Piero Hincapie can. We all worried about William Saliba needing a long lay-off after the World Cup, but the arrival of Ezri Konsa offset that in exemplary fashion. If we miss Declan Rice, we have two World Cup winners, a Brazilian international, and one of the most highly regarded young English midfielders around to fill that gap. Further forward, Noni Madueke is performing at a level that makes Bukayo Saka’s absence feel less impactful than it would have previously, and while I think forward line quality remains an concern we need to solve as urgently as January, you can flip a coin between most of our options there without feeling you’ve weakened yourself considerably.

It has been revealed that unfortunately, I don’t think the same applies between the sticks. Raya has been the stand-out goalkeeper of the last few years, establishing himself as Arsenal’s number 1 after an initial settling in period. One, by the way, which I don’t think the manager handled particularly well. Typically he’s been near flawless in terms of his man-management, and while he was fundamentally right about wanting the Spaniard to come in and take the position to a new level, the way he fudged things around Aaron Ramsdale, talking about how he’d sub a goalkeeper in a game and all that nonsense really wasn’t his best moment. It left both of his keepers in a weird place for too long, until Raya’s confidence grew and his quality came to the fore.

Since then he’s won multiple golden glove awards, his shot-stopping has been incredible at times, and although every player and every keeper will make mistakes, his have been few and far between. For me though, despite the eye-catching acrobatics – which are more easily clipped up for the social media generation – his key asset is the assurance he brings to the team. Not just when he has the ball at his feet (even if there are times I would like him to move it more rapidly), but how good he is from opposition set-pieces and crosses. He comes and claims and eases pressure time and time again, and I think that’s the thing we’re going to miss most if he’s out for any significant period of time.

It has been revealed that kepa is obviously a very experienced second choice, but is second choice for a reason. Realistically though, I don’t think there’s much any club can do to have a back-up option that’s nearly as good as their number 1. If you’re being brutally honest, many clubs in the Premier League don’t have a first choice that comes anywhere close to be as good as Raya, despite their best efforts and spending millions to try and find that player. So, as anxious as I am about him being out, it is one of those things we can’t really complain about. We just have to get on with it.

Sources indicate that as I remarked in yesterday’s blog, we are probably going to be less secure at the back, that feels kind of inevitable, so the onus on the players further forward increases. Score more goals, turn that domination of possession and territory into more chances. If we have the ball in their half, our goalkeeper becomes something of a non-issue for as long as that’s the case. There are ways to cope, but we might need to gird our loins for some iffy moments at the back that we haven’t had to experience too often of late.

In a recent development, as Arsenal fans though, we’ve come through worse than this with goalkeepers in the past. I don’t want to give anyone PTSD first thing on a Monday morning, but when you’ve lived what we’ve lived in seasons gone by, hopefully a little Kepa period won’t be too traumatic. And maybe, after the scan, there’ll be better news about Raya than we expect. Fingers crossed.

According to recent reports, right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. In a recent development, pod should be out around noon. Until then!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vincenzo Montella’s time with AC Milan was ‘a dream’ for him, but he failed to achieve much during his time at the helm.

Looking back on Montella’s time leading Milan is tricky. On paper, the Italian had a strong tenure at the club, achieving a 50% win rate and only losing 18 of his 64 games in charge at San Siro, not a terrible record by any means.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, he even ended a five-year trophy drought with a win against Juventus in the Supercoppa Italiana and returned the Rossoneri to Europe, with a sixth-place finish in the 2016/17 season. In itself, that was a first since 2014.

Sources indicate that this is where context matters, though. The start of the 2017/18 season was tough, as the Diavolo won six of their first 14 games and he was sacked before December. Despite that, he still views the club in an excellent light.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport’s ‘La Tripletta’ podcast, Montella went over his time with the club and how he fulfilled a dream by taking the job, as MilanPress relays.

“It was a fantastic experience there [at Milan] too, it was my dream. Then, as a professional, it’s a little different, but when I was thirteen I was a fan of that AC Milan team. My older brother took me to see Maradona’s Napoli team twice to make me a Napoli fan, and Maradona scored three goals.

“Despite this, my idol was Van Basten because I was a striker: I studied him and dreamed of becoming like him, and so I was a Milan fan. I knew everything about Milan, so for me it was an incredible feeling to join Milan.”.

It has been revealed that “He liked to talk about football; he liked to give advice even when it was a bit out of context at the time, because he always had the mentality of having Van Basten as a centre forward with Papin, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner, on the bench. He wanted me to play with two strikers, and I tried to plug the gap for months.

According to recent reports, “I told him it was difficult; I knew all the lineups of those years. I was a Milan fan: the starter was Van Basten and the reserve was Papin, both Ballon d’Or winners. So, ‘If you buy me some players like that, rest assured that I’ll play them both.'”.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a year when we returned to Europe. I think it had been two or three years since Milan had been there, and it was something new at the time. We won a trophy, a small one. Just the other night I saw Galliani at a dinner; he reminded me of it and remembers it perfectly.

“I have to say that I found him to be the perfect manager at the time, because he was always on my side when it came to pressure; he gave me complete autonomy in my decisions and he helped me with everything, from the number of collaborators to new things; whatever I asked for, he was always on the coach’s side.

“And so for me he was truly an incredible manager, who in that phase, in that change, was fundamental even in achieving these small results, especially after Berlusconi’s great AC Milan.

“We deserved to win even in regulation time: we had some easy chances to win it, then it came to penalties. Gigio saved the penalty from Dybala, who kicked it really hard, but he filled the net with it.”.

According to recent reports, “I was a little worried from the beginning because there was this obsession with publicising everything, almost like a publicity stunt, so I was a little worried. In theory, there was sharing, at least that’s what it looked like, but I couldn’t back out when in reality that wasn’t always the case.

Recent findings suggest that “And so sometimes there were players I hadn’t even consulted about, who would arrive and then say, ‘It was shared,’ and when you’re there, you can’t say otherwise. Certainly, when you build a team and have the budget, the first thing you do is: we had a goalkeeper, I’ll get a centre forward, we were missing a centre forward.

“In the final selection, the centre forward was the only one left, with a budget of 15-20 million. And then Kalinic… yes, I chose him because that was the final budget. So our, let’s say, second-choice striker was paid thirty-eight million, if I remember correctly, who was André Silva, and the first striker was paid half that.

“And so, in my opinion, a misunderstanding of this kind was created, with so many changes, even though at that stage we weren’t even playing badly for having fifteen upcoming players.

“We still had Calhanoglu, who wasn’t feeling well, coming off months of suspension. The team was still being built: we weren’t in line with the Scudetto objectives that had been announced, but certainly, given our development, we were absolutely on target.

“Who would I have signed up front? At the time, we were probably negotiating for Aubameyang, if I remember correctly. Ronaldo? No, I didn’t believe it, not at all.”.

Recent findings suggest that "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat stated. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a big relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

Industry observers note that themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

According to recent reports, "I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

Industry observers note that growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," said Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

Industry observers note that "I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat said. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

Family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

It has been revealed that "I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat mentioned. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a substantial change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

According to recent reports, as well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat said, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat said.

Industry observers note that "So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she mentioned. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

It has been revealed that that has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

"The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

In a recent development, should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she said.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Ever since Fabinho left in 2023, fans have demanded that new players were brought in by the Anfield outfit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool's midfield has been a major topic of conversation for a while now.

Ever since Fabinho left in 2023, fans have demanded that new players were brought in by the Anfield outfit.

Obviously, that still hasn't happened with Arne Slot and Andoni Iraola actually making Liverpool's midfield weaker thanks to their sales of Tyler Morton and Curtis Jones over the last couple of seasons.

In the summer, most fans thought that at least one midfielder would be brought in to replace Jones but, instead, Trey Nyoni was given a more prominent role.

And, while he's done well this term, since he's still so young, he can't be playing two 90 minute games every week which is why a fresh midfielder now needs to be brought in.

Gavi could be Liverpool's surprise solution to their problems.

Over the last few years, many different players have been discussed as potential options for Liverpool to explore.

Recently, Lamine Camara, Adam Wharton and Alex Scott have been the most linked with an Anfield switch.

However, in the upcoming January transfer window, each of them will only be available for crazy high fees.

And, with how many clubs have shown an interest in acquiring their services, there's going to be a huge battle for every single player.

That's why this latest update from journalist Juan Jesus is exciting.

"In addition to Alejandro Balde, Barça are now pushing Gavi out this very winter to fund the signing of a centre-back, seen as the club’s absolute priority," he wrote.

"The main target to bolster the defence is Nico Schlotterbeck, but the current wage bill leaves no room to pull off a move of that magnitude in January.

"To comply with financial fair play rules and try to sign him in this winter window, the board is pushing for two key sales: Balde on one hand, and the bombshell departure of Gavi on the other.".

Gavi would be perfect for Liverpool.

At the start of the 2026-27 season, nobody thought that Gavi would become available on the market.

He's been a regular feature in Flick's intends for as long as anyone can remember and, since he's only 22 years old, there's so much of his career left to go.

Obviously, a deal wouldn't come cheap for the Spaniard but, if the La Liga giants are as strapped for cash as they seem to be, an agreement could probably be reached.

Gavi can also play as a number 10, eight or six which is massively beneficial for the Reds.

This versatility coupled with his endless experience of the Champions League and La Liga all join together to make him the perfect player for Liverpool to sign.

Here's hoping that an agreement can be reached.

Dortmund a tricky test + Guimaraes on getting to grips with Arteta’s midfield

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal are in Champions League action this evening, taking on Borussia Dortmund at home.
  • He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious.
  • We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at that moment, and the first test that we’ve done showed something that is much more encouraging.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal are in Champions League action this evening, taking on Borussia Dortmund at home. It’s a game that Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in the absence of David Raya, but the news around the Arsenal number 1 was a little more positive than expected. In his press conference yesterday, Mikel Arteta mentioned:.

He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected.

We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at that moment, and the first test that we’ve done showed something that is much more encouraging. There’s no need for surgery, which was the main fear especially because that would rule him out for months, so let’s see.

Sources indicate that so, it seems like he’s going to miss a few games, but not anything prolonged, which is obviously good news. Elsewhere, there’s room for rotation, and I think this might be a good chance to give minutes to William Saliba who hasn’t played competitively since the World Cup. He’s had a couple of behind closed doors appearances, which will be useful in terms of fitness, but nothing compares with actually playing at this level.

I wonder too if players like Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie will fancy their chances, but that seems like a lot of change in the back four – and the goalkeeper – so we’ll have to wait and see there. In midfield, we can bring Myles Lewis-Skelly in for a start, but obviously the manager has plenty to choose from in there, and up front I imagine it will be a chance for Viktor Gyokeres whose minutes have been scant so far this season. Asked if the striker had been knocking on his door about that, Arteta noted:.

No, we have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing, to gather information about the way they are feeling, and so far, it’s been very positive with Viktor and with the rest of the team.

According to recent reports, he could really use a goal tonight if he does start, as does Christos Tzolis whose numbers so far this season aren’t where you’d like them to be. Obviously there’s more to assessing a player than simply goals and assists, but for a left winger brought into replace two players who contributed a lot to the team over the last few seasons, just two assists from 11 appearances (Community Shield excluded) is a little below what you’d hope. He has had an injury, of course, but if his season needs a kick-start, tonight would be very timely.

Dortmund sit top of the Bundesliga right now, unbeaten in the league thus far, and with just one defeat all season in all competitions. That did come in the Champions League, away to Bodo Glimt, but this will be a tricky test tonight for Arsenal. Arteta states:.

I’m very impressed with them, you see the results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga at the top and where they are in the Champions League and especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat they are able to create. We had them here in pre-season, and they showed the quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that. But we play at home in front of our crowd, and now we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

In a recent development, after a disappointing second half against Newcastle on Saturday, I’m sure the manager will be looking for a response from his side. It’s nice to be at home again, and a long spell of games in London will hopefully less taxing physically without all the travel, so it’d be good to get that off to a winning start tonight.

Elsewhere, Bruno Guimaraes spoke about his first few months at the club, and how he now feels like he’s getting to grips with what Mikel Arteta wants from him, saying:.

I’m here, I don’t know, three, four months? It’s still a lot to go, but I now definitely understand my role in the team, the way that Mikel wants me to play in the team. So, yeah, I think I still can play much, much better.

According to recent reports, and it’s quite interesting to hear him talk about how at Arsenal he is more ‘free’ than he was under Eddie Howe at Newcastle. Most would feel it was the other way around, but he explained:.

According to recent reports, it’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

It has been revealed that if you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.

It has been revealed that I think there’s more to come from him, he’s looked good at times, a little off the pace at others, and I think my main worry is about the physical side of his game. Does he have the running power and athleticism that enables players like Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to thrive under this manager? At 29, he’s no spring chicken, but I guess there’s always room for improvement. Anyway, his press conference stuff from yesterday is worth reading, and there’s some good chat about him on the Arsecast Extra which you’ll find below.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

AC Milan put on arguably their best display of the Ruben Amorim era so far as they beat Frosinone 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

It has been revealed that gabriele Calvani’s early own-goal kicked off what would be a miserable night for the Canarini, before Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. Patrizio Masini’s goal halved the deficit, and kept the game open going into the second half.

It was a win that Milan needed to move back into the top four, also given that only Inter out of the top six sides in the table dropped points. Rohit Rajeev has the tactical breakdown from the win.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Milan once again deployed a modified version of their 3-4-2-1, with Bartesaghi operating on the left. Alvini, meanwhile, had to cope without his striker Raimondo and opted for a 3-5-2, pairing Ghedjemis and Kvernadze up front.

Recent findings suggest that frosinone made their intentions clear from the opening seconds. Goalkeeper Palmisani immediately played a direct ball into a targeted zone, with Frosinone committing several players towards the expected landing area to create a numerical advantage and win the aerial duel.

Milan built from deep with three players at the back, while Maignan pushed forward to act as an additional centre-back. This created a 4v3 in the first line of build-up, forcing Frosinone’s front three of Ghedjemis, Kvernadze and Schmid to press deeper.

Their movement opened up space between Frosinone’s first and second pressing lines for Milan’s players to receive.

However, it was Rabiot’s movement that proved decisive in creating the overload for Milan’s opening goal. With Frosinone committing three forwards to the press and keeping two players wide, only two midfielders and three defenders remained to deal with Milan’s build-up.

Although Musah and Rabiot were initially marked, Rabiot dropped deeper into midfield to create a numerical advantage and free himself to receive possession.

It has been revealed that this movement directly contributed to Milan’s opening goal. Rabiot dropped between the lines to receive possession, forcing Cittadini to step out of his defensive position and follow him.

Rabiot then laid the ball off to Modric, who immediately played it into the space vacated by Cittadini. Under pressure, Frosinone inadvertently turned the ball into their own net to give Milan a 1-0 lead.

Frosinone looked to commit numbers into Milan’s half, creating ball-sided overloads to progress through the pitch. Their two wingers maintained wide positions to stretch Milan’s wing-backs and create more space in the central areas.

Out of possession, Frosinone adopted a 3-4-3 to match Milan’s 3-4-2-1 in possession. They also maintained a very high defensive line, looking to press Milan aggressively and win the ball back as high up the pitch as possible.

Milan allowed Frosinone to dictate possession, dropping into a deeper defensive block to invite them into their half. Once Frosinone advanced, Milan looked to win the ball back and launch quick counter-attacks.

In a recent development, frosinone’s lack of a clear attacking structure and, more importantly, an organised rest defence left them vulnerable in transition. Milan exploited this disorganisation repeatedly, with the next four goals all benefiting from the spaces Frosinone left behind.

Industry observers note that the second goal perfectly illustrated Milan’s approach in transition. Frosinone had committed ten players into Milan’s half, leaving very little defensive cover behind.

Recent findings suggest that ramos won possession, and Musah immediately played a vertical pass to release Moreira through on goal. Moreira and Rabiot then drew three recovering defenders towards them before creating the space for Ramos to finish.

In a recent development, frosinone’s high-risk approach briefly paid off with Masini’s goal. They drew Milan into central areas before pressing aggressively to recover possession. With their players positioned close together, they were able to combine promptly and progress the ball towards Kvernadze.

A deflection off De Winter then took the ball into Ghedjemis’ path, allowing him to set up Masini for the finish.

Sources indicate that frosinone consistently targeted Milan’s left flank, particularly the space around Bartesaghi. The individual duel between Ghedjemis and Bartesaghi became a key feature of the game.

Recent findings suggest that ghedjemis repeatedly beat his marker in 1v1 situations and posed a threat. Recognising the problem, Amorim took Bartesaghi off at half-time.

Recent findings suggest that after the break, Jashari and Pulisic began making coordinated counter-movements. Pulisic dropped deeper, drawing his marker away and creating space in the wide attacking area, which Jashari then exploited with an advancing run.

The goal was very similar to the movement Jashari made against Venezia, highlighting a recurring pattern in Milan’s attacking play.

Both Cisse’s and Pulisic’s goals came from a counter-attack following a Frosinone corner, for which they did not leave many men back.

For Cisse’s finish, his body orientation suggested he was going to shoot towards the goalkeeper’s right, prompting the keeper to adjust his stance accordingly. Cisse then went the other way, finding the opposite corner.

Recent findings suggest that so, perhaps everything can be taken with a pinch of whatever type of salt fits your narrative. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one problem ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • Sources indicate that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one problem ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Sources indicate that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already said he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, mentioned in a note.

"I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

Some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, noted the vote showed the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of big tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

Sources indicate that "This election reveals that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he remarked. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

If the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown said, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

Sources indicate that that sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

"Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

Trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard said, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump noted in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election issue — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

"You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard said. "From a political point of view, that's the most important thing now.".

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he said in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and concerns.

In a recent development, yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another issue vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the new Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

It has been revealed that "Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard said. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.
