Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (748 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

The first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

Since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

At that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, mentioned additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

Sources indicate that "Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler remarked. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

According to recent reports, "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," mentioned Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

Recent findings suggest that LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," said BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

Sources indicate that this year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," said Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," said Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

In a recent development, A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

Calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob indicates three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

Sources indicate that passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

In a recent development, roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

It has been revealed that spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

Recent findings suggest that calcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

Recent findings suggest that city want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement. They first asked in August and City refused, while Gazzetta dello Sport says Luciano Spalletti wants competition for Andrea Cambiaso.

Industry observers note that city paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly. He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

His strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

The weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

No, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Maresca has used Nico O’Reilly in midfield this season, yet O’Reilly started only seven of City’s first 15 games while managing a back problem, so an available specialist left-back is no luxury. Khusanov, Nunes and Guéhi all picked up knocks at Forest, which leaves the back line short.

Sources indicate that city should treat the Juventus talks as a pricing exercise. A straight loan sends a 25-year-old on a contract until 2030 away for six months and returns him no more valuable, so only a loan with an obligation to buy close to the £31m fee makes sense.

Otherwise, give him a league start, see whether his attacking threat helps a side that keeps conceding, and let Maresca’s evidence decide. A club that paid £31m for a left-back last year has not shown he cannot do the job; it has shown only that the manager prefers somebody else.

Racing de Santander will be bidding to continue their excellent run of form when they head to Estadi Ciutat de Valencia on Friday evening to tackle Levante.

Levante just about lead the overall head-to-head record between these two sides, winning 11 of their 30 meetings in all competitions, suffering 10 defeats in the process.

Levante have a record of two wins, six draws and five defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them down in 15th spot in the La Liga table.

The Frogs have been an entertaining watch at home this season, scoring 14 times and conceding 13, boasting a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Luis Castro's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-1 draw with Elche, while they also drew 0-0 with Celta Vigo before the November international break, with their last victory coming at home to Athletic Bilbao on October 21.

Levante finished 16th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27, but they have found it difficult to win matches so far this term.

The Frogs actually beat Racing 3-1 in the last match between the two teams in April 2025, but two of their last four meetings have been won by the latter.

Racing, who are the reigning Segunda Division champions, have been one of the stories of the season in Spain's top flight, impressing hugely on their return to La Liga.

The Green and Whites boast a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats from their 13 league matches, which has left them seventh in the table on 17 points.

Jose Alberto's side have actually conceded 32 times in La Liga this season, which is comfortably the worst record in the division, but they have found the back of the net on 20 occasions - the sixth-best attacking record at this stage.

Racing will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Real Sociedad, and they have now been victorious in three of their last four in the league, and four of their last five in all competitions.

The Green and Whites have struggled away from home this season, though, losing five of their six league matches, only managing to pick up three points.

Roger Brugue has scored five times and registered one assist in 13 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set for a spot in the starting side.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players.
  • This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.
  • Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had mentioned he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

In between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Sources indicate that fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX.

Industry observers note that A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

"Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz.

Recent findings suggest that tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

Tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

In a recent development, the missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

According to recent reports, kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Industry observers note that neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Leaving it until the 88th minute, when the game had already been killed by Tel, to send on the striker was a clear error.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

It has been revealed that chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee let out an incredibly loud “for f---’s sake” when one corner routine went wrong. Nobody could hear what he was shouting over the Tottenham celebrations when Penders scored his own goal, but it would almost certainly have started with “f” again.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

Maddison had scored a brilliant goal on his first league start in 18 months against Coventry, but he had to be replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Gallagher at Stamford Bridge.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa.

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Recent findings suggest that tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

Industry observers note that “I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso remarked. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”.

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”.

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

According to recent reports, but Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He mentioned: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”.

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

Sources indicate that “We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi mentioned. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”.

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”.

A long-awaited Stamford Bridge victory for @SpursOfficial 👏 https://t.co/Qqwgbuj3Y3.

“When we have dinner together and spend time together in the dressing room, I see a different group, different relationships and a different atmosphere among the players.

“The character was great today, but we have many, many upcoming players. The players who stayed here from last season and two or three seasons ago suffered from the results, including two 17th-place finishes.

“We are working to change the last part of the club’s history. We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room and many great players. I think if we work hard, we can do something notable.

“The week in Marbella, speaking face to face, opening ourselves up and removing the mask, was important for the spirit and belief.

“The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more key than the tactics.”.

Industry observers note that speaking to Sky Sports, the Tottenham boss noted: “It was a big moment for the fans, the club and the players. They deserved this win and prepared very well.

“We are improving a lot in our mentality, as a group and in our relationships with the players. We are also improving on the pitch.

In a recent development, “Against Aston Villa and Everton, for 30 minutes we were playing very well. Maybe we didn’t score because our finishing wasn’t good enough, and perhaps in the first difficult moment we changed our mentality.

“Now we are a complete team. The players are playing better and we have improved our style.

“I have to believe in this group. I never lost confidence in my players.

“We have to keep working hard and improving. We have many great players, and I believe we can do something key if we continue in this way.”.

Tottenham have a rare and fully deserved victory over 10-man Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. An own goal from Penders and Tel’s brilliant solo strike sealed the three points for De Zerbi’s side. Chelsea produced a dreadful performance with Palmer sent off in the second half to compound a miserable evening for the hosts.

Three GLORIOUS points at Stamford Bridge 🤩 https://t.co/czWx6bUB78.

Chelsea supporters have emptied Stamford Bridge. Tottenham fans are making all the noise. The visitors have been better in every department on the pitch today.

Spurs are on their way to a historic win at Stamford Bridge. Tel starts a dribble from inside his own half, escapes Acheampong and glides past Lacroix, before arrowing a clinical effort into the bottom corner, sending De Zerbi and the away support absolutely wild. Incredible scenes. Chelsea have been miles off the pace today.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina.
  • The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.
  • Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina. Spalletti's side now go into the international break outside the Champions League places, with their next home game brought forward by a day.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

The hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

The closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

Recent findings suggest that at his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti mentioned he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything important. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

Next up for Juventus is Venezia, who sit 19th on 6 points. When fixture times were first set, that game was pencilled in for Monday 23 November at 20:45 Italian time.

Arsenal eye Serie A’s 11-goal striker: Should they pay £26m?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (411 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Footballtransfertavern

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested.
  • Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals.
  • According to recent reports, finishing is the selling point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested. The 21-year-old Portugal forward has scored 11 goals in 11 Serie A games since joining from Benfica B in July. Barcelona are equally keen, Inter watch him live at every match, and Napoli are reported as his strongest Italian suitor.

The interest makes sense. Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals. Arsenal’s results haven’t suffered, but their number nine position has produced little.

According to recent reports, finishing is the selling point. FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes. The weaknesses are just as clear: he wins 34% of his duels, completes 41% of his dribbles and ranks in the ninth percentile among forwards for defensive contribution, which clashes with the pressing Arteta wants from his striker.

In a recent development, di Marzio claims Monza will listen at around £22m to £26m, with the money earmarked for other signings, after paying about £3m including bonuses. Flashscore reports Benfica hold a 20% sell-on and a right to match offers, and Varela’s agents meet Monza this week.

Yes, but in the summer and only if Gyokeres leaves. Arsenal’s results are strong, so a January rush for a 21-year-old would add risk without fixing a crisis. A fee near £26m looks modest beside the £64m Gyokeres cost, and Varela’s goals-per-game record argues for the gamble far more than Gyokeres’ two in 15 does.

The real risk is suitability. He also scores for a struggling side, so his chances come in games unlike most of the Premier League games Arsenal play. Arteta needs a number nine who presses and wins duels, and Varela does neither well, so Arsenal would be buying a finisher and building the rest of his game themselves.

That is workable if Varela arrives as competition for Havertz rather than the first choice. Arsenal should also expect resistance beyond the price, because Benfica’s matching right and Inter’s summer plans complicate any early bid.

Watching him until June costs Arsenal nothing, and another 20 league games will show whether this form is real or a hot streak.

#106167. An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 120 min read (24050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~120 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2.
  • Recent findings suggest that the bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2.
  • Industry observers note that conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

Recent findings suggest that the bulk of crop production worldwide strictly depends on rainfall to support irrigation needs, and limitations on water availability pose a global challenge for agricultural productivity, with water scarcity and drought stress incurring unpredictable and potentially catastrophic effects on yield1,2. The adverse effects of climate change on crop productivity have historically been underestimated5. With the average global temperature expected to increase by 1.5–2.0 °C by 2050, the frequency and severity of drought events will be further increased, which could be accompanied by 30–40% reductions in food production3,4. Despite facing the greatest food-security challenges in the modern era7,8, annual crop yield improvement rates have not kept pace with projected food demands, that is, a 50–70% increase to accommodate approximately 9.8 billion people worldwide by 2050 (ref. 9), further compounding the effects of disaster events and decreasing availability of arable land.

Industry observers note that conventional plant-breeding efforts have boosted crop yields in water-limited environments, for example, through improved stress resistance, greater biomass accumulation, delayed leaf senescence or ‘stay-green’ strategies7,10, but broad potential remains for improving yield and yield stability across growing regions regardless of water availability11,12. Increasingly precise genetic modification strategies have advanced crop engineering for drought resistance13,14,15,16,17. For example, heterologous expression of a rice trehalose-6-phosphate phosphatase in developing maize ears improves yield under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions in the field16. In cassava, expressing a modified Arabidopsis potassium (K+) channel in vascular tissues improves K+ transport, photosynthesis and root biomass, allowing enhanced productivity in nutrient-poor and drought-prone environments17. However, genetic modification usually cannot provide a single, universal solution to multifactorial drought stress, and this approach frequently fails to improve yields in the field13,18 because drought resistance is a complex quantitative trait involving a multitude of small-effect loci or genes mediating diverse stress responses, such as stomatal closure (for reduced transpiration) or modified root architecture (for enhanced water uptake)10,19. Drought resistance typically accompanies trade-offs by way of reduced yield in the absence of stress6,20, undermining the effectiveness of certain genetic modification strategies. Therefore, of the genes identified in controlled conditions that often show limited effects in real-world environments, relatively few undergo rigorous field trials to properly demonstrate consistent agronomic value21.

Recent findings suggest that among known genetic resources for drought resistance, lichens have been generally overlooked despite their ubiquitous distribution across extreme ecological niches. In arid-adapted lichens, mycobionts appear to contribute more to survival under water deficit than photobionts22,23. We have previously isolated the lichen-forming fungus Endocarpon pusillum, which has extreme drought resistance. Exposure to dehydration stress identified 1,781 differentially expressed E. pusillum genes24. Through mining those data, here we identified the transcription factor gene EpTFIIAγ that broadly enhances yield and biomass production under field conditions when heterologously expressed in the world’s top-three-produced staple cereal crops of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), maize (Zea mays L.) and rice (Oryza sativa L.). EpTFIIAγ delays plant senescence, enhances photosynthetic capacity, water-use efficiency (WUE) and drought resistance by functioning as a transcriptional co-factor to coordinately target multiple genes and pathways. EpTFIIAγ binds to TATA-box-containing motifs and interacts with several endogenous wheat transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance networks involved in stress responses, plant development, photosynthesis and grain yield. Our results provide an unprecedented broad-spectrum resource for crop improvement and highlight the untapped potential of lichen mycobionts as sources of versatile transgenes for biotechnology.

It has been revealed that among 25 differentially expressed genes predicted to encode transcription factors identified under dehydration stress in E. pusillum (Fig. 1a), EPUS02736 exhibits the strongest upregulation and encodes a transcription initiation factor IIA γ-chain (designated EpTFIIAγ). EpTFIIAγ shares homology with TFIIAs from plants, such as Arabidopsis, wheat, rice and maize, although the genetic relatedness between EpTFIIAγ and these homologues is relatively distant (Fig. 1b). Strong expression under dehydration stress implicates EpTFIIAγ in drought adaptation of the lichen mycobiont. Towards understanding its functionality, EpTFIIAγ was expressed in the yeast ∆hog1 mutant (deficient in HOG1, which encodes the high osmolarity glycerol 1 protein kinase), resulting in remarkably enhanced growth on solid synthetic dropout (SD) −Ura medium with 0.75 M sorbitol (Fig. 1c), and statistically significantly higher growth in corresponding liquid medium than the control (Fig. 1d). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ contributes to regulating osmotic stress.

According to recent reports, a, RNA-seq analysis of 25 transcription factor genes in E. pusillum under osmotic stress. FC, fold change; FPKM, fragments per kilobase of transcript per million mapped fragments. b, Phylogenetic analysis of EpTFIIAγ (red) and homologues from Arabidopsis, rice, maize and wheat. Bootstrap values are shown at the nodes and branch lengths are indicated by the scale bar. c,d, Osmotic stress resistance of ∆hog1 yeast expressing TFIIAγ from E. pusillum, wheat and Arabidopsis on SD−Ura medium ± 0.75 M sorbitol (c) and time course of culture density (d). n = 4 biological replicates. e, Transgene expression (top left), rosette morphology (bottom left) and survival (right) of Arabidopsis Col-0 and EpTFIIAγ lines under well-watered (WW) and drought-stress (DS) conditions. Anti-EpTFIIAγ and β-actin were used for immunoblotting. n = 3 independent experiments. Scale bars, 2 cm. f–j, Transgene expression, plant morphology and survival under WW and DS conditions in five wheat cultivars and their corresponding EpTFIIAγ lines: Fielder (f), XN979 (g), XN511 (h), JM22 (i) and XZ9104 (j). n = 3 (f) and 4 (g–j) independent experiments. Images were acquired before water withdrawal and after 3 days of rewatering following approximately 25 days of drought treatment. Scale bars, 2 cm. k,l, Field images of wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ transgenic wheat under full-irrigation (k) and water-limited (l) conditions. Scale bars, 10 cm. TL, transgenic line. m,n, Grain yield per plot under full-irrigation (m) and water-limited (n) conditions. n = 4 plots. Data are mean ± s.d. Statistical significance was assessed using two-sided Student’s t-test (d), Brown–Forsythe and Welch analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by two-sided Dunnett’s T3 test (e–j), and one-way ANOVA followed by two-sided Dunnett’s test (m,n). *P < 0.05 and **P < 0.01 indicate statistically significant differences. Gel source data are shown in Supplementary Fig. 25.

To determine whether EpTFIIAγ could also enhance drought resistance in plants, we first expressed endogenous TFIIAγ genes from Arabidopsis and wheat in the yeast hog1 mutant; however, no obvious effect on osmotic stress tolerance was observed (Fig. 1c), suggesting that TFIIAγ genes probably mediate divergent biological functions between plants and E. pusillum. We then generated three genetically independent transgenic Arabidopsis lines (TL1–TL3) constitutively and heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ and examined drought resistance. To our surprise, seedlings expressing EpTFIIAγ had survival rates approximately seven times higher than wild-type Col-0 controls under drought-stress conditions (Fig. 1e). This improved drought resistance was not limited to the eudicot Arabidopsis. Transgenic wheat cv. Fielder seedlings heterologously expressing EpTFIIAγ from the strong and constitutive Ubiquitin promoter showed an approximately 3.5-fold increase in survival rate compared with wild-type Fielder under drought stress (Fig. 1f). However, overexpression of endogenous AtTFIIAγ or TaTFIIAγ in their respective native hosts had no such positive effect on drought resistance (Extended Data Fig. 1a–f), supporting their functional divergence from EpTFIIAγ. Analysis of key drought-resistance traits, including root architecture and biomass production (Extended Data Fig. 1g–o), stomatal density and aperture, and leaf water loss and transpiration (that is, leaf temperature; Extended Data Fig. 1p–u and Supplementary Fig. 1), suggested that the enhanced drought resistance among EpTFIIAγ transgenic Arabidopsis and wheat lines was mainly attributable to enhanced root growth and decreased stomatal aperture and transpiration compared with wild-type controls. Transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat seedlings over-accumulated abscisic acid, auxin and salicylic acid hormones than wild-type Fielder plants under drought stress, whereas their accumulation remained comparable with that of controls under well-watered conditions (Supplementary Fig. 2).

Drought resistance varies widely across wheat germplasm25. To understand whether EpTFIIAγ can endow major commercially relevant wheat cultivars in China with enhanced drought resistance, we generated four genetically independent transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines in each of cvs. Xinong979 (XN979), Xinong511 (XN511), Jimai22 (JM22) and Xingzi9104 (XZ9104), which show different degrees of stress resistance and yield25,26. Greenhouse drought-resistance assays revealed that survival rates were 2–3 times higher for transgenic lines than corresponding wild-type controls (Fig. 1g–j), whereas stomatal aperture, leaf water loss rates and transpiration were also decreased in transgenic lines under drought stress (Supplementary Figs. 3 and 4). Therefore, heterologous EpTFIIAγ expression consistently endowed drought resistance and key physiological changes across four additional wheat cultivars. EpTFIIAγ plants also displayed broad-spectrum resilience to heat stress, lodging and multiple races of the major wheat stripe-rust fungal pathogen Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici (Extended Data Fig. 2), further supporting potential EpTFIIAγ deployment for engineering stacked resistance to environmental stressors in wheat.

In a recent development, certain transgenes are known to improve resistance to drought stress but at the undesirable expense of reduced plant growth or productivity, known as yield drag13,18,20. We examined performance of all five sets of transgenic EpTFIIAγ wheat lines to identify potential yield drag in 3-year field trials under full-irrigation and water-limited conditions with a rain shelter in Yangling, China, which is characterized by a warm temperate semi-humid and semi-arid climate with 200–400 mm of rainfall during the growing season (Supplementary Fig. 5). All tested EpTFIIAγ lines had consistently increased grain yield across different genetic backgrounds and years compared with respective wild-type controls under full-irrigation control conditions. This increase was more pronounced under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1k–n; Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6–9). In 2025, grain yields surpassed that of the two previous years under water-limited conditions for EpTFIIAγ lines because of the higher temperature, lower rainfall and severe drought stress (Supplementary Fig. 5). Across all five backgrounds, EpTFIIAγ lines displayed 7.6–13.9% increases in grain yield per plant and 7.9–13.5% increases in yield per plot relative to controls under full-irrigation conditions, and increases of 22.3–38.3% in yield per plant and 19.4–32.8% higher yield per plot under water-limited conditions (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Fig. 7c,i). EpTFIIAγ lines were taller, had increased plant biomass, grain length, grain width and grain weight relative to respective wild-type controls, potentially contributing to increased plot yields. Despite higher grain yields, EpTFIIAγ plants had similar straw weight compared with wild-type plants, resulting in 6.1–14.8% higher harvest indices (that is, ratio of grain yield to aboveground biomass) under full irrigation and 7.6–15.5% increases in harvest indices under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). Growth duration was similar between genotypes under full irrigation, whereas time to maturity was 2–5 days longer for EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than maturation time in the wild-type under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Fig. 7f,l), reflecting adaptation to drought stress.

To evaluate trait stability, additional field trials were conducted in 2025 in three arid growing regions in China (Heyang, Shaanxi; Linfen, Shanxi; and Cangzhou, Hebei) with rainfall of 120–250 mm during the growing season. Grain yield per plant for EpTFIIAγ lines increased by 10.9–25.6% compared with wild-type controls, with the highest yield increases (15.6–25.6%) observed in Heyang (Supplementary Tables 4–6). These results underscored the potential of EpTFIIAγ as a valuable genetic resource for developing drought-resistant, high-yield wheat varieties in elite backgrounds regardless of water availability. In detail, EpTFIIAγ plants had expanded flag leaves, accelerated grain filling, larger pericarp cells, higher starch granule density and increased starch biosynthesis relative to wild-type controls under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Extended Data Fig. 3 and Supplementary Fig. 10). This accelerated filling led to heavier grains beginning at 5 days after flowering, regardless of water conditions, resulting in 3.3–8.8% greater final grain weight in well-watered EpTFIIAγ plants and 15.2–21.4% higher grain weight in drought-stressed transgenic plants than in their respective wild-type controls (Fig. 1m,n, Supplementary Tables 1–3 and Supplementary Figs. 6 and 7). These improvements were consistent with the higher sucrose, glucose and fructose levels, as well as increased sucrose synthase, cell-wall invertase and ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase activities observed in EpTFIIAγ grains during the early filling stage (Extended Data Fig. 4). Conversely, flag-leaf sheaths of EpTFIIAγ plants had lower levels of these sugars than wild-type controls. These results suggested that the extended duration and enhanced rate of grain filling may be key determinants of increased final grain weight and yield in EpTFIIAγ plants.

Given the drought resistance and yield boosts endowed by EpTFIIAγ in transgenic wheat lines, we examined which physiological processes are altered. EpTFIIAγ plants had delayed senescence compared with controls under water-limited conditions (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9), which we hypothesized might be due to increased WUE. We also hypothesised that carbon assimilation might be altered given that increases in yield and biomass require enhanced carbon fixation. To examine possible differences in water status and carbon assimilation between wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ plants, we first used plant multispectral imaging to estimate normalized difference vegetation index and normalized water index values at seedling stage in a growth chamber. Transgenic plants indeed had higher normalized difference vegetation index and lower normalized water index values than Fielder plants under both well-watered and drought-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 11). EpTFIIAγ seedling leaves had lower 13C fractionation than Fielder during the 18 days of drought treatment following water withdrawal (Fig. 2a), indicating enhanced WUE in these transgenic plants. These results are consistent with the lower water loss rate and transpiration for EpTFIIAγ plants under drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 1p–u).

Instantaneous WUE (iWUE) is defined as the ratio of the photosynthetic rate relative to the transpiration rate. For each genotype, the sample sizes under full-irrigation and water-limited conditions were 21 and 22 plants (d), 20 and 30 plants (e), 25 and 21 plants (f), and 22 and 23 plants (g), respectively. h–j, Root phenotypes (h,i) and quantification of root biomass (j) of Fielder and EpTFIIAγ plants at the grain-filling stage under full-irrigation and water-limited field conditions. n = 10 plants (j). The boxplots show the median (centre line), 25th–75th percentiles (box limits) and minimum and maximum values (whiskers), with individual data points overlaid. Statistical significance was determined by one-way ANOVA with two-sided Dunnett’s multiple comparison test. *P < 0.05 and **P < 0.01 indicate statistically significant differences. Exact P values for comparisons shown as P > 0.99 are provided in the Source Data for Fig. 2.

In a recent development, to further assess the effects of EpTFIIAγ expression on carbon assimilation, we measured quantum yield of photosystem II photochemistry (ΦPSII). Transgenic EpTFIIAγ seedlings had approximately 14.6% higher ΦPSII than Fielder control plants under well-watered conditions, and approximately 29.9% greater ΦPSII under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b). These results suggested that EpTFIIAγ expression led to enhanced maintenance of PSII activity. EpTFIIAγ plants had improved light–response and CO2–response curves of net photosynthesis (Fig. 2b,c). In addition, the abundance of PSI, PSII, cytochrome b6/f and LHC proteins, as well as RuBisCO subunits were all increased in transgenic plants under well-watered or drought-stress conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5d). RuBisCO activity was increased in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 5c), which agreed with A–Ci curves showing higher maximum rates of RuBisCO carboxylation and electron transport (Extended Data Fig. 5e–h). Consistent with these increases, EpTFIIAγ leaves over-accumulated sucrose, glucose, starch and soluble sugars (Extended Data Fig. 5i), further demonstrating enhanced carbon assimilation in these plants. Of note, drought stress triggered a marked accumulation of root soluble sugars (for example, sucrose, glucose and fructose) in EpTFIIAγ plants compared with Fielder, whereas no such difference was observed under optimal conditions (Extended Data Fig. 5j), aligning with enhanced root growth under drought stress.

Industry observers note that we next evaluated how EpTFIIAγ contributes to lifting photosynthetic capacity in field-grown plants. Chlorophyll content (soil and plant analyser development, SPAD), maximum quantum yield of PSII photochemistry (Fv/Fm) and photosynthetic rate were all enhanced in EpTFIIAγ transgenic plants in all five wheat cultivars compared with their corresponding wild-type controls at all of the tillering, stem elongation, flowering and milk development stages under both full-irrigation and water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 12–17). However, stomatal conductance and transpiration rate were lower in transgenic plants under water-limited conditions, although some EpTFIIAγ lines had slightly higher stomatal conductance under full-irrigation conditions. In agreement with these results, WUE (that is, the ratio of net photosynthetic rate to transpiration rate) was improved in EpTFIIAγ plants under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2d–g and Supplementary Figs. 14–17). Under full-irrigation field conditions, no obvious phenotypic changes in root development were seen between wild-type Fielder and transgenic plants. By contrast, all EpTFIIAγ lines had increased root length and biomass compared with Fielder under water-limited conditions (Fig. 2h–j), aligning with the stay-green phenotype observed in shoots (Supplementary Figs. 8 and 9). Together, field-grown EpTFIIAγ wheat lines have enhanced WUE, resulting in slower water consumption, delayed senescence under water-limited conditions, and consequently more extensive root development, thereby facilitating greater water uptake. These data also suggested that enhanced photosynthetic capacity and CO2 assimilation contributed to the increased biomass and grain yield observed in EpTFIIAγ wheat plants.

Eukaryotic transcription initiation by RNA polymerase II (Pol II) requires numerous general transcription factors and cofactors to nucleate at core promoter sites, which typically contain several DNA sequence elements (for example, TATA boxes), to form the pre-initiation complex27. Among them, the transcription initiation factor TFIIA is a general cofactor that acts as an anti-repressor or co-activator27,28. In multicellular eukaryotes, the TFIIA complex typically comprises α-subunit, β-subunit and γ-subunit, encoded by TFIIAαβ and TFIIAγ genes27,29. To characterize the function of EpTFIIAγ, we first examined TFIIAγ sequences across species. EpTFIIAγ retains a conserved protein architecture while also harbouring a unique, lineage-specific N-terminal extension (Supplementary Table 7 and Supplementary Fig. 18). To determine whether EpTFIIAγ participates in transcription initiation, we first examined its subcellular localization in wheat protoplasts. EpTFIIAγ–GFP mainly localized to the nucleus, whereas intact TaTFIIAγ–GFP and AtTFIIAγ–GFP fusions revealed both nuclear and cytoplasmic localization (Extended Data Fig. 6a,b). To investigate whether EpTFIIAγ could interact with endogenous TFIIAαβ to form the TFIIA holocomplex in plants, we conducted yeast two-hybrid, luciferase-complementation imaging and pulldown assays. These experiments consistently demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ fails to detectably interact with either wheat or Arabidopsis TFIIAαβ, whereas both TaTFIIAγ and AtTFIIAγ could interact with their corresponding TFIIAαβ proteins to form complete TFIIA complexes (Extended Data Fig. 6c–g). These results indicated that EpTFIIAγ does not appear to function as a transcription initiation factor in plants, or at least does so differently from these expression hosts.

Industry observers note that the TFIIA recognition element (IIARE) located upstream of the TATA box enhances recruitment of TFIIA and other components to activate transcription at TATA-box promoter motifs27,29. We asked whether EpTFIIAγ could similarly bind to such recognition sites. Electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could indeed directly bind to an IIARE-containing TATA box, whereas neither wheat TaTFIIAγ nor Arabidopsis AtTFIIAγ displayed detectable binding (Extended Data Fig. 6h,i). Although fungal and plant TFIIAγ proteins share conserved α-helical and β-sheet architectures, EpTFIIAγ uniquely harbours an N-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR; Fig. 3a). Hypothesizing that this region may confer specialized biological function, we generated an IDR deletion variant (EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR)). This truncation did not bind to IIARE-containing TATA-box fragments, and likewise, its nuclear localization was impaired (Fig. 3b,c and Extended Data Fig. 6j). Conversely, fusing the EpTFIIAγ-derived IDR to TaTFIIAγ or AtTFIIAγ conferred binding to probes carrying an IIARE-containing TATA box (Fig. 3b and Extended Data Fig. 6j).

Scale bars, 5 μm. Fluorescence recovery and diffusion curves are shown in the bottom panels. d, Density heatmaps of ChIP–seq peaks flanking the transcriptional start site (TSS) throughout the wheat genome expressing EpTFIIAγ–HA. ChIP–seq was performed with two independent biological samples. Rep, replicate; RPKM, reads per kilobase of transcript per million mapped reads. e, Genomic distribution of EpTFIIAγ–HA-binding regions identified in wheat. UTR, untranslated region. f, Venn diagram of candidate EpTFIIAγ target gene numbers overlapping between two ChIP–seq biological replicates. g, Enrichment of TATA-containing motifs in promoter regions identified in ChIP–seq peaks. h, Gene Ontology analysis of candidate EpTFIIAγ targets identified in panel f. i, EMSAs of MBP–EpTFIIAγ binding to TATA-box-containing promoter fragments from eight selected genes: TaDREB1C, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaCOG1, TaYCF9, TaCP47 and TaGAPC1. j, ChIP–qPCR analysis of EpTFIIAγ–HA enrichment at promoters of the indicated genes. k, Dual-luciferase assays testing EpTFIIAγ transactivation of the promoters of the eight candidate target genes. Data are mean ± s.d. from four biological replicates (j,k). Experiments were independently repeated three times with similar results (b,i). Statistical significance was determined by two-sided unpaired Student’s t-tests. **P < 0.01 indicates statistically significant differences. Gel source data are shown in Supplementary Fig. 25.

To test whether this IDR could drive liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), we expressed EpTFIIAγ–GFP in Nicotiana benthamiana leaf epidermal cells. Upon hyperosmotic stress, EpTFIIAγ maintained a homogeneous nuclear distribution and did not coalesce into condensates under either stress or non-stress conditions (Supplementary Fig. 19a). Moreover, His–EpTFIIAγ did not detectably form dynamic droplets in vitro, indicating that its relatively short IDR was insufficient to trigger LLPS (Supplementary Fig. 19b). Further evaluation of chromatin-binding dynamics through fluorescence recovery after photobleaching and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy showed that EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) exhibited markedly shallower bleach depth and accelerated recovery kinetics (Fig. 3c and Supplementary Fig. 19c–h), indicating attenuated chromatin association and higher mobility than full-length control. Stable-transgenic EpTFIIAγ(ΔIDR) expression in wheat cv. Fielder conferred no obvious improvement in drought resistance relative to wild-type (Extended Data Fig. 6k–m), indicating that the IDR is indeed indispensable for EpTFIIAγ function in the drought-stress response.

In a recent development, to identify EpTFIIAγ-binding sites across the wheat genome, we performed chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP–seq) with transgenic plants stably expressing EpTFIIAγ–HA in the cv. Fielder (Fig. 3d). Across two replicates, 17,131 putative EpTFIIAγ-binding sites were identified, 85% of which are in intergenic regions and 15% in genic regions, including gene bodies as well as the 3-kb upstream and 300-bp downstream flanking sequences presumed to harbour the promoter and transcriptional terminator, respectively (Fig. 3e). Analysis of 2,570 genic binding sites identified 1,347 annotated genes bound by EpTFIIAγ–HA (Fig. 3f and Supplementary Table 8), and the core motif within these binding regions was enriched with a TATA-containing element (Fig. 3g). Gene Ontology analysis found that these EpTFIIAγ–HA target genes were enriched in terms related to stress responses, such as ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’, ‘response to cold’, ‘regulation of stomatal movement’ and ‘transpiration’; hormone responses, such as ‘response to abscisic acid (ABA)’, ‘response to auxin’ and ‘response to brassinosteroid’, as well as ‘photosynthesis’ and ‘chlorophyll biosynthesis’ (Fig. 3h). Further EMSAs confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could bind to promoter regions of 387 wheat genes, underscoring its capacity to regulate diverse biological pathways in planta, such as those related to stress response, development, photosynthesis and yield formation (Extended Data Fig. 7a, Supplementary Table 9 and Supplementary Fig. 20).

To define the regulatory network involved in the effects of EpTFIIAγ on photosynthetic efficiency, WUE and the drought-stress response, we compared transcriptomes of 20-day-old wild-type Fielder and EpTFIIAγ transgenic seedlings. This identified 1,953 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; fold change of more than 2 or less than 0.5, P < 0.05) in transgenic plants relative to Fielder, including 1,405 upregulated and 548 downregulated DEGs (Extended Data Fig. 7b–g and Supplementary Table 10). By examining overlap between ChIP–seq and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, we identified 1,056 candidate target genes that are potentially bound and transcriptionally regulated by EpTFIIAγ, including 824 upregulated and 232 downregulated genes in EpTFIIAγ plants (Extended Data Fig. 8a,b). Among them, stress-response-related genes involved in ABA and drought responses demonstrated strong enrichment (Extended Data Fig. 8c), such as wheat homologues of Arabidopsis MYBR1 (ref. 30), FBH4 (ref. 31) and DREB1C32 (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10). Other genes known to function in plant development, source–sink partitioning and grain yield were also present among upregulated DEGs, including the CONSTANS-like gene TaCol-B5 (ref. 33), wheat homologues of rice OsCIN2 (ref. 34) and OsSWEET4 (ref. 35), and homologues of Arabidopsis VND7 (ref. 36) and SWEET12 (ref. 37). Among photosynthesis-related DEGs, we found TaYCF9 and TaCP47, which are homologues of Arabidopsis PsbZ38 and CP47 (ref. 39) encoding subunits of the PSII reaction centre. In addition, we identified TaCOG1, a homologue of the Arabidopsis Dof transcription factor COG1, that promotes biomass accumulation by enhancing photosynthetic capacity40. TaGAPC1, a redox-dependent regulator of energy metabolism that mediates stress responses in Arabidopsis41, was also upregulated (Supplementary Tables 9 and 10).

MBP–EpTFIIAγ could bind in vitro to approximately 30-bp promoter fragments containing TATA motifs from TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1, and this interaction could be compromised by competition from unlabelled probes (Fig. 3i, Extended Data Fig. 8d and Supplementary Fig. 21a). ChIP–quantitative PCR (qPCR) indicated that these promoter fragments indicated greater enrichment in EpTFIIAγ–HA genomic DNA precipitated by anti-haemagglutinin antibody than by the immunoglobulin G (IgG) control (Fig. 3j and Extended Data Fig. 8e), demonstrating that EpTFIIAγ could indeed bind to TATA-containing core promoter motifs. In dual-luciferase reporter assays using approximately 1.5-kb promoter fragments, activities of target promoters were upregulated in the presence of EpTFIIAγ compared with empty vector controls (Fig. 3k, Extended Data Fig. 8f and Supplementary Fig. 21b), supported by real-time (RT)–qPCR analyses revealing that TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 mRNAs were all expressed at higher levels in all three EpTFIIAγ transgenic lines than in wild-type Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 8g). These results collectively indicated that EpTFIIAγ functions as a transcriptional cofactor to regulate target gene expression.

To determine how downstream regulatory targets contribute to enhancing drought resistance, photosynthetic efficiency and grain yield in EpTFIIAγ plants, we generated transgenic wheat lines overexpressing TaDREB1C, TaCOG1 or TaCIN2 in the cv. Fielder background. TaDREB1C lines had enhanced drought resistance and WUE through accelerated stomatal closure and reduced transpiration compared with Fielder under drought stress (Extended Data Fig. 9a–g). This overexpression did not detectably alter growth period, which remained comparable with controls under full irrigation (Extended Data Fig. 9h–j). Plants overexpressing TaCOG1 had enhanced photosynthetic and carbon-fixation capacities, resulting in increased biomass and grain yield relative to controls (Extended Data Fig. 9k–p). Moreover, TaCIN2 overexpression resulted in accelerated grain filling, ultimately increasing grain size and yield (Extended Data Fig. 9q–v). These results position the EpTFIIAγ regulon as pivotal for concurrently improving drought resilience and yield potential in wheat.

In a recent development, to investigate the mechanisms through which EpTFIIAγ drives enhanced drought resistance, photosynthetic capacity and grain yield, we conducted yeast two-hybrid screening using a cDNA library obtained from wheat cv. Chinese Spring seedlings. Four successive rounds of screening with EpTFIIAγ serving as bait yielded 112 candidate interacting proteins (Supplementary Table 11), including 22 putative transcription factors. After repeating yeast two-hybrid assays to confirm that EpTFIIAγ could interact with wheat homologues of Arabidopsis transcriptional activators WRKY46 (ref. 42), AKS1 (ref. 43), ARF6 (ref. 44) and VOZ1 (ref. 45) (Fig. 4a), luciferase-complementation imaging tested whether EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these partners. Co-expression of EpTFIIAγ–C-terminal luciferase fragment (cLUC) with N-terminal luciferase fragment (nLUC)–TaWRKY46, nLUC–TaAKS1, nLUC–TaARF6 or nLUC–TaVOZ1 produced chemiluminescence, whereas no signal was observed in regions infiltrated with vector controls (Fig. 4b). Bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays further showed that co-expression of the EpTFIIAγ–cYFP with nYFP–TaWRKY46, nYFP–TaAKS1, nYFP–TaARF6 or nYFP–TaVOZ1 led to obvious YFP signal (Fig. 4c and Supplementary Fig. 22a,b). Pulldown assays indicated that MBP–EpTFIIAγ could interact with GST–TaWRKY46, GST–TaAKS1, GST–TaARF6 and HA–TaVOZ1 in vitro (Fig. 4d). Co-immunoprecipitation assays in N. benthamiana leaves co-expressing 35Spro:GFP–EpTFIIAγ and 35Spro:mCherry–TaWRKY46, 35Spro:mCherry–TaARF6 or 35Spro:mCherry–EpTFIIAγ with 35Spro:GFP–TaAKS1, 35Spro:GFP–TaVOZ1 also confirmed that EpTFIIAγ could physically interact with these transcription factors in planta (Fig. 4e). By contrast, the IDR-deleted EpTFIIAγ variant failed to detectably interact with any tested partners (Supplementary Fig. 22c,d), highlighting the essential role of this IDR. Moreover, no interactions were observed between wheat TaTFIIAγ and the transcription factors TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1 (Supplementary Fig. 22e,f), underscoring EpTFIIAγ functional specificity.

a, Yeast two-hybrid assays of EpTFIIAγ physical interactions with four wheat transcription factors. BD–p53 and AD–SV40-T served as a positive control and BD–Lam and AD–RecT were used as a negative control. SD−T–L, SD medium without Trp and Leu; SD−T–L–H–A, SD medium without Trp, Leu, His and Ade. b, Luciferase complementation imaging of EpTFIIAγ interactions with the indicated wheat transcription factors. Scale bars, 50 μm. d, In vitro pulldown assays of MBP–EpTFIIAγ interactions with GST-tagged or HA-tagged wheat transcription factors. Western blotting of precipitated fractions was conducted with anti-GST, anti-HA or anti-MBP antibodies. e, In vivo co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) assays of interactions between EpTFIIAγ and TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1. Pulldowns used GFP–EpTFIIAγ, GFP–TaAKS1 and GFP–TaVOZ1 immobilized on GFP resin beads, and anti-mCherry antibody was used for western blotting. Input blots included both anti-mCherry and anti-GFP antibodies. f, EMSA testing whether EpTFIIAγ enhances DNA binding in vitro of four wheat transcription factors (TFs). g, Dual-luciferase assays reporting cooperative or additive effects of EpTFIIAγ upon co-expression with four wheat transcription factors in activating target promoters. Statistical significance was determined by two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. **P < 0.01 indicates statistically significant differences. Gel source data are shown in Supplementary Fig. 25.

In a recent development, to map genome-wide binding sites and target genes, we used CUT&Tag in stable-transgenic cv. Fielder plants expressing TaWRKY46–HA, TaAKS1–FLAG, TaARF6–HA or TaVOZ1–HA. Integrative analysis identified 467, 309, 495 and 505 target genes that are potentially co-bound and co-regulated by EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, respectively (Supplementary Table 12 and Supplementary Fig. 23), suggesting direct involvement in the EpTFIIAγ regulatory network. GST–TaWRKY46 could bind in vitro to probes containing the W-box from the TaCol-B5, TaSWEET4 and TaSWEET12 promoters, and these binding events increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Similarly, GST–TaAKS1 could bind to probes harbouring the G-box or E-box from the TaDREB1C, TaCol-B5, TaYCF9 or TaCOG1 promoter regions, with the addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ markedly strengthening these interactions in vitro. Moreover, GST–TaARF6 could interact with AuxRE-containing probes derived from the TaYCF9, TaFBH4 and TaCIN2 promoters, which was boosted by addition of MBP–EpTFIIAγ, whereas GST–TaVOZ1 bound to probes with a 5′-CTTCTT-3′ motif present in the TaCP47, TaVND7, TaMYBR1 and TaGAPC1 promoter regions, which also increased in the presence of MBP–EpTFIIAγ (Fig. 4f and Extended Data Fig. 10a). Dual-luciferase reporter assays indicated that TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 could activate genes with corresponding promoter recognition sites (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b).

To determine whether EpTFIIAγ functions coordinately with or independently of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 in regulating target genes, we performed dual-luciferase reporter assays. Upon co-expressing EpTFIIAγ with each respective transcription factor, LUC activity driven by the TaDREB1C, TaFBH4, TaMYBR1, TaVND7, TaCol-B5, TaCIN2, TaSWEET4, TaSWEET12, TaYCF9, TaCP47, TaCOG1 and TaGAPC1 promoters was greater than the expression of wheat transcription factors alone (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 10b). To clarify whether activation of these transcription-factor genes contributed to the observed drought resistance of transgenic EpTFIIAγ plants, we examined drought resistance in lines overexpressing TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 (Extended Data Fig. 11a–d), as well as wrky46-knockout and arf6-knockout mutants by gene editing in cv. Fielder (Extended Data Fig. 11e,f). All overexpression lines had enhanced drought resistance relative to Fielder, whereas both mutants had compromised drought resistance compared with Fielder controls (Extended Data Fig. 11g–j). To further characterize the genetic interactions of EpTFIIAγ with TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1, we crossed EpTFIIAγ plants (Fielder background) with each overexpression line. Under normal conditions, homozygous double-transgene-positive progeny of all crosses bore phenotypes comparable with that of TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 and TaVOZ1 overexpression plants. By contrast, double-transgene-carrying hybrids revealed stronger drought resistance than control plants expressing a single transgene (Extended Data Fig. 11k,l). These findings collectively demonstrated that EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with select transcription activators, such as TaWRKY46, TaAKS1, TaARF6 or TaVOZ1, and that their interactions resulted in additive effects on EpTFIIAγ target gene expression, consequently enhancing the drought response, photosynthesis and grain yield.

Sources indicate that to determine whether EpTFIIAγ function in conferring drought resistance was conserved in other major cereal crops, we generated three transgenic EpTFIIAγ lines each in rice cv. Nipponbare and maize inbred line B73 backgrounds (Fig. 5a,b). In greenhouse drought-resistance assays, survival of transgenic EpTFIIAγ rice and maize lines was extended by approximately 2.6-fold and approximately 2.8-fold for rice (Fig. 5c,d) and maize (Fig. 5e,f), respectively, compared with their wild-type controls. Transcriptomic analysis found that genes involved in ‘transcriptional regulation’, ‘response to ABA’, ‘response to water deprivation’, ‘response to osmotic stress’ and ‘photosynthesis’ were enriched among upregulated DEGs in EpTFIIAγ seedlings of both species (Extended Data Fig. 12a,b and Supplementary Tables 13 and 14).
